- VAULT: content/PROJECTS/AGENTIC-SYSTEMS/Marketing Agent Research.md (2026-08-25) - PR-as-approval-gate, the Kestra RESUME and Cloudflare waitForEvent traps, the GitHub required-reviewers limitation, read-only reference memory, English-only anti-slop gates failing on Polish, faststylometry's diacritic bug, PersonalBench on LLM judges, the Bielik/PLLuM licensing split, and the Article 50 scope correction - [own prior work, NOT independent]
- VAULT: content/BUSINESS/KNOWLEDGE/INFO/Social Media Algorithms - Maximizing Reach in 2026.md - per-platform originality and demotion mechanics (Meta March 2026 account-wide non-recommendability, Instagram's 40-60% repost penalty and the 10-reposts-in-30-days rule, LinkedIn relative signal weights) - [vault compilation]
- VAULT SIBLING: results/RAG-grounded_post_generation.json - the retrieval half of this workflow; its corpus-governance section is the GDPR counterpart to this item's Article 50 section - [sibling research item]
- VAULT SIBLING: results/Synthetic_persona_pre-testing.json - the pre-publication screening layer that sits immediately before this gate - [sibling research item]

#### fit

**platform and format fit**

Cross-referencing 'Social Media Algorithms - Maximizing Reach in 2026' rather than re-deriving ranking mechanics.

WHERE THE GATE MATTERS MOST:
- LINKEDIN. Highest stakes by a wide margin: the highest measured AI density (30% short-form, 41% long-form per Pangram; 81.2% long-form per Originality.ai), the most explicit enforcement posture, an account-level pattern-based detection approach, and a private inauthenticity flag that makes the penalty invisible from outside. This is the platform the gate is designed for.
- REDDIT. The gate is not optional here, and it is not algorithmic: many subreddits ban AI-generated posts outright, AutoModerator rules enforce it, and the community downvotes what slips through. Note the structural contrast in the Pangram data - Reddit runs 3% short-form / 13% long-form AI, and only 1.7% on replies, an order of magnitude below LinkedIn. Reddit's gate is social and it works.
- SUBSTACK NOTES. Relationship-based recommendation; generic content is punished by low engagement rather than by a classifier, which is slower and harder to diagnose.
- BLUESKY. No central AI-slop downranker (there is no algorithmic feed to demote in), but a strongly anti-AI culture plus community labellers mean the penalty is social: reports, blocks, and being hidden by subscribers.

WHERE IT MATTERS LESS, OR DIFFERENTLY:
- X. The published home-mixer scoring code shows the demotion machinery aimed at spam, policy violations and negative downstream reactions rather than at AI authorship as such. The gate still pays, but through different signals.
- INSTAGRAM / TIKTOK / FACEBOOK. For TEXT, low relevance - captions are short and the classifiers are aimed elsewhere. For the VISUAL layer, high relevance and a different regime: C2PA and SynthID provenance, platform auto-labelling, and Article 50(4) first-subparagraph deep-fake duties, which have NO human-review carve-out. A gate covering text does not cover an AI avatar or a cloned voice.

BY FORMAT:
- LONG-FORM TEXT POSTS AND ARTICLES: highest risk and highest return. This is where AI density is concentrated and where the substance the gate forces in has room to show.
- CAROUSELS / DOCUMENT POSTS: high risk and a specific one - the format is fully automatable end to end, so a gate that only checks the text misses the deck. Extend Gate 2 to the slides.
- SHORT VIDEO: the text gate is nearly irrelevant; the synthetic-media regime replaces it entirely.
- COMMENTS: an under-gated surface and, per Pangram, 23.7% AI on LinkedIn. LinkedIn blocks hundreds of thousands of automated comment attempts daily. The gate should cover comments, and almost nobody's does.

WHERE IT BACKFIRES: nowhere, in the sense that the gate never makes a post worse. It backfires only on VOLUME - a real gate caps your output at the rate your non-substitutable inputs arrive, which for most people is well below the 2-5 posts per week the cadence literature recommends. That tension is real and is dealt with under scales_with.

**audience fit**

B2B / TECHNICAL: highest value and highest stakes. This audience has the sharpest detectors (they read a lot of generated text professionally), the longest memory, and the highest cost of being caught - your buyers are people who will judge your engineering by your posts. It is also the audience most likely to test a claim in the comments, which is exactly what Gate 1 (provenance) protects you from.

B2C / GENERAL: lower stakes, and this is where the conflicting evidence bites hardest - Originality.ai's category breakdown shows AI-shaped inspirational content OUTPERFORMING human content by ~75% per post. A strict gate is a genuine competitive sacrifice in the inspiration/motivation lane. Make that trade knowingly, not by accident.

PL AUDIENCE - three specific things, all from Marketing Agent Research and all silent failures:
1. English-only anti-slop tooling (sloptrim, content-quality-scorer.py) returns CLEAN on Polish slop. If your gate has an automated component and your track is Polish, that component is lying to you.
2. faststylometry's default token pattern deletes every word containing a Polish diacritic and still returns confident numbers. Patch `tok_match_pattern` or do not use it.
3. For automated Polish post-correction, Bielik is Apache-2.0 and commercially safe; PLLuM is CC-BY-NC-4.0 and is not.
Consequence: on the PL track the gate must be MORE human, not less - the automated half is unavailable.

EN AUDIENCE: the automated half of the gate works, but the audience is more saturated and more detection-literate. The bar for what counts as a non-substitutable specific is higher.

CROSS-CUTTING: the gate is audience-neutral in its logic and audience-specific in its threshold. What counts as a claim worth sourcing depends entirely on what your readers already know.

**scales with**

WHAT DOES NOT CAP IT: account size, follower count, network position. A 200-follower account runs the identical gate for the identical benefit - and on the AI-citation objective specifically, Semrush found sub-500-follower creators cited comparably to large ones, so the gate's citation return is genuinely follower-independent.

WHAT CAPS IT, in order of how binding it actually is:
1. THE SUPPLY OF NON-SUBSTITUTABLE INPUTS. This is the real ceiling and the one people refuse to look at. You can only publish what you have actually done. For an active consultant the rate of genuinely forwardable first-hand specifics is roughly 2-4 per month. A gate demanding one per post therefore caps you at 2-4 gated posts per month unless you either (a) do more publishable work, (b) mine an existing corpus you have not yet published from - exactly what the RAG-grounded sibling item is for, and usually the cheapest unlock - or (c) accept a mixed cadence where gated substance posts anchor a larger number of lighter commentary posts.
2. YOUR ATTENTION. The gate is the bottleneck by design. This is a feature, and it is also why it degrades: the pressure to publish converts the gate into a click within about three weeks unless the rejection rate is monitored.
3. TEAM SIZE - but only in one direction. Drafting scales with headcount; editorial responsibility does not, because under the Commission's framing a named person holds ultimate legal responsibility and their identity and contact details must be publicly available. For a solo creator that person is you and cannot be anyone else.
4. CORPUS SIZE. A large, well-indexed body of your own prior work makes Gates 1 and 2 cheap; a thin corpus makes every post expensive.

THE OBJECTIVE-DEPENDENT CEILING WORTH NAMING: the gate's return is much higher on the AI-CITATION objective than on the VIRALITY objective. Citation rewards exactly what the gate produces (original, educational, verifiable, consistent) and is indifferent to follower count; virality rewards emotional and structural properties the gate does not touch. If your objective is reach velocity, the gate is insurance. If your objective is being cited, the gate is the strategy.

THE CADENCE TENSION, stated plainly: Marketing Agent Research already flagged that 15 posts per month across two brands is below the 2-5 per week effectiveness threshold from a 4.8M-post analysis. A strict gate makes that worse before it makes it better. Resolve it by raising input supply, not by lowering the gate.

**decay and saturation**

SHELF LIFE: the longest in this research, and the direction is unusual - the gate APPRECIATES.
- LEGAL LAYER: years. Primary legislation; no decay.
- PLATFORM LAYER: quarters. Every specific enforcement detail here is a 2026 snapshot.
- COMPETITIVE VALUE: RISING. AI density on LinkedIn long-form sits somewhere between 41% and 81% depending on whose detector you believe, and has roughly doubled year over year on Originality.ai's numbers. Scarcity of human writing is the gate's return, and it increases without any effort from you.

WHAT DOES DECAY, and it is worth being precise about which parts:
1. Any DETECTOR-EVASION tactic. 'Remove the em-dashes, vary the sentence length' is a 6-12-month edge at best and is the wrong game entirely - it optimises the tell rather than the substance, and the substance is what the classifiers are moving toward.
2. Any specific TOOL BEHAVIOUR. The Kestra and Cloudflare defaults will change; re-audit annually.
3. The specific PREVALENCE NUMBERS. Quote them with dates or not at all.

THE SATURATION RISK THAT IS REAL is a ritual risk rather than a market risk: if 'human-in-the-loop editorial protocol' becomes a marketed compliance checkbox - and given the Article 50 timing it will - the FORM will spread and the SUBSTANCE will not. Everyone will have a gate; most gates will pass everything. The differentiator then collapses back onto the only thing that cannot be copied: whether you actually have a proprietary number, a real incident, a named project. Which is to say the gate never saturates as long as its content requirement is real, and it saturates instantly if the requirement becomes 'a human looked at it'.

THE ONE THING THAT WOULD KILL IT: reliable, cheap, platform-side per-document AI detection that classifies on authorship rather than on quality. That would make the gate's substance requirement irrelevant and replace it with a provenance requirement. No credible sign of this in 2026 - detection remains population-level - but it is the scenario to watch, and the Code of Practice's 2027-02-02 detection-interoperability milestone is the date at which to look again.

#### risk

**failure modes**

Nine, ordered by how often they actually happen. Note that the first three all produce a gate that LOOKS installed.

1. RUBBER-STAMP DRIFT. The gate is honoured for three weeks and then becomes a click. Universal, gradual, and invisible from inside. THE ONLY RELIABLE DETECTOR IS THE REJECTION RATE: if you have not binned a finished draft in a month, your gate has already failed. Instrument this before anything else.
2. TIMEOUT-AS-APPROVAL. The orchestrator publishes when the human does not answer. Kestra `Pause` defaults to `behavior: RESUME`; Cloudflare Workflows `waitForEvent` has a 24-hour default and the vendor's own HITL example proceeds with a default action on expiry. This is the most dangerous failure in the entire item because it fails silently, passes every demo, and is indistinguishable from a working gate until the day you are busy.
3. POST-REVIEW AI TOUCH. Someone runs a final polish after the human edit. It reintroduces the cadence tells you just removed AND, per Orrick's reading of the Commission guidelines, can void the Article 50 exception. Utterly natural to do; you must make it a rule, because judgement will not catch it.
4. FORM-CHECKING INSTEAD OF SUBSTANCE-CHECKING. The gate asks 'did a human read this?' rather than 'what did the human add that the model could not?'. This is precisely the distinction the Commission drew when it excluded spell-checking, and it is the difference between a protocol and a ritual.
5. SELF-GRADING. The model checks its own output and passes almost everything. Adjacent failure: using an LLM judge to gate VOICE, which PersonalBench showed rates texts as varied where stylometry says they are not.
6. LANGUAGE-BLIND AUTOMATION. English-only linters return clean on Polish. A false pass in the safety component.
7. CHECKLIST INFLATION. A 25-item gate is not run. A 10-item gate is. Every item you add lowers the probability the whole thing executes; this is a real trade-off, not a counsel of laziness.
8. NO RECORD. You have a gate, you run it, and you cannot prove it. Fine for quality, fatal for the Article 50 position, which requires you to evidence review and to name a responsible person with published contact details.
9. TEMPLATED HUMAN INPUT. The human contribution is always the same shape - always an anecdote, always a number, always the same three-beat story. That is a template, and templates are exactly what a cross-post pattern detector is best placed to catch. The gate then produces branded genericness, which is worse than unbranded genericness because it is consistent.

WHAT FAILURE LOOKS LIKE FROM OUTSIDE: nothing. There is no error message for any of these. That is the argument for instrumenting the gate's own health rather than waiting for the reach signal that will never arrive.

**ai slop risk**

The gate is the MITIGATION for slop everywhere else in this research, so the interesting question is the gate's own slop risk - and it has one.

RISK 1 - AN AI-DRAFTED GATE. Ask a model to write you an editorial checklist and you get fourteen items of the form 'Ensure the content aligns with your brand voice'. Unfalsifiable, unrunnable, and it will pass every draft. THE TELL: no item in the checklist can fail. A real gate item names a specific artifact that must exist.

RISK 2 - TEMPLATED HUMAN INPUT (the serious one). Once you require one non-substitutable specific per post, the cheapest way to satisfy the requirement is to always supply the SAME KIND of specific. Every post opens with a client anecdote; every post carries one number; every post turns on the same beat. You have then manufactured a signature. LinkedIn's described detection looks at patterns across a member's content, so a consistent shape is the worst possible thing to standardise on. MITIGATION: rotate the input TYPE deliberately across the five categories in human_input_required, and check the shape across your last ten posts rather than within one.

RISK 3 - THE GATE AS CONTENT. Publishing your editorial protocol is itself an attractive post topic in 2026, which means it is already saturated. A post about having a gate is not evidence of having one.

THE SPECIFIC TELLS THAT A GATE IS NOT WORKING, observable in the output:
- Every post passes on the first run.
- Numbers appear without sample sizes or dates (Gate 1 is not running).
- The 'personal' element is generic enough to be true of anyone in your role (Gate 2 is not running - run the substitution audit and watch it survive).
- Perfect structural symmetry across posts: same paragraph count, same emoji positions, same transition words week after week.
- The post contains a strong claim and no mechanism - assertion where a reason should be.
- Nothing in the post could embarrass you if wrong. Real first-hand content carries risk; that is what makes it non-substitutable.

**human input required**

THIS FIELD IS THE ITEM. Everything else is scaffolding around it.

THE MINIMUM, AS A CHECKABLE GATE. Every post must contain AT LEAST ONE of the following, and the type should rotate across posts:
(a) A NUMBER YOU PRODUCED, stated with its sample size, time window and one-line method. Not a number you read - a number you made. 'Across 31 research items at 75 fields each, 156 values came back flagged uncertain' is this. 'Studies show 70% of marketers...' is not.
(b) A FIRST-HAND INCIDENT WITH A DATE AND A CONSEQUENCE. Not 'I once worked with a client who' - a specific thing, on a specific date, that cost a specific amount of time or money or trust.
(c) A NAMED ARTIFACT YOU ACTUALLY TOUCHED: a client (with permission), a repo, a tool at a specific version, a config value, an error message. Version numbers and exact strings are extremely hard to fake and extremely easy to verify, which is what makes them good evidence.
(d) A JUDGMENT CALL WITH ITS COST STATED. 'We chose the Agent SDK over managed agents and gave up zero idle cost to get it' - a decision, an alternative, and what the decision cost. Models produce recommendations; they do not produce regrets.
(e) A CORRECTION OF YOUR OWN EARLIER PUBLIC POSITION. The single strongest form, because it requires a prior position and the willingness to revise it in public.

PLUS, UNCONDITIONALLY, three things that are not content but are gates:
- THE FALSIFICATION ANSWER. Without opening a model, you must be able to answer: what would make this post wrong? If you cannot, you do not understand the claim well enough to publish it.
- THE SUBSTITUTION AUDIT MUST FAIL. Swap your name and numbers for a competitor's; if the post survives intact, there is nothing of yours in it.
- THE DEFENCE. You must be able to answer the sharpest likely comment yourself, in public, without going back to a model.

THE LEGAL MINIMUM, which is a separate and lower bar - satisfying it does not satisfy the quality bar above. Per the Commission's Article 50 FAQ (24 July 2026): human review means 'deliberate examination of the substance of the content by one or more natural persons possessing relevant knowledge', comparable to academic peer review or professional validation; editorial control means a responsible editorial entity with 'the authority to approve, alter or reject' on substantive grounds including fact-checking; and editorial responsibility means a person holding 'ultimate legal responsibility over the publication of the content', whose identity and contact information are publicly available. Explicitly excluded: 'superficial, solely formal, or procedural checks (e.g. spell-checking or grammatical correction)'.

WHY THIS IS ALSO THE RANKING ANSWER: the NLP classifiers the platforms describe are not detecting authorship, they are detecting the ABSENCE of exactly these properties - perspective, specificity, stake. LinkedIn's own phrasing, 'appears AI-generated and lacks clear perspective', names the second half as the operative test. Which means the quality gate, the compliance gate and the reach gate are, for once, the same gate.

**policy and legal**

ASSUMING A POLAND/EU-BASED CREATOR. Four layers.

LAYER 1 - THE EU AI ACT, ARTICLE 50. Applicable since 2026-08-02.
The obligation: 'Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest shall disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated.' (Art. 50(4), 2nd subparagraph.)
THE CARVE-OUT, verbatim: the obligation does not apply 'where the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control and where a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication.' Two conditions, CONJUNCTIVE - both must hold.
THE COMMISSION'S OPERATIVE DEFINITIONS (Article 50 transparency FAQ, 24 July 2026):
- HUMAN REVIEW = 'deliberate examination of the substance of the content by one or more natural persons possessing relevant knowledge', with academic peer review and professional validation given as examples.
- EDITORIAL CONTROL = control exercised in practice by a responsible editorial entity (an editor-in-chief is the example given) having 'the authority to approve, alter or reject' on substantive grounds INCLUDING FACT-CHECKING.
- NOT SUFFICIENT: 'superficial, solely formal, or procedural checks (e.g. spell-checking or grammatical correction)'. This is the sentence that turns this entry from a slogan into a gate, and it is why Gate 3 requires a substantive diff rather than an edit.
- EDITORIAL RESPONSIBILITY = 'ultimate legal responsibility over the publication of the content, including the human review or editorial control', and per Orrick the responsible person's identity and contact information must be publicly available.
- ORRICK'S ADDITIONAL POINT, operationally the sharpest: 'substantive AI intervention occurring after human review can cause the exception to be voided.' Sequencing is load-bearing.
MATTERS OF PUBLIC INTEREST, per the Commission: politics, democratic processes, public administration, justice, law enforcement, fundamental rights, security, health, environmental protection, consumer safety, and 'economic, financial, political, scientific, or cultural developments that may be relevant subject of public debate'. Ordinary marketing and personal-brand content is NOT covered as such - Marketing Agent Research recorded this as an explicit correction to an earlier, broader reading in the vault. But the scientific/technical limb is broad and the boundary is untested (see conflicting_evidence).
PENALTIES: Article 99(4) - up to EUR 15,000,000 or 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is HIGHER. Article 99(6) - for SMEs and start-ups, whichever is LOWER. For a Polish solo consultancy the operative figure is 3% of turnover.
OUT OF SCOPE FOR THE TEXT GATE: Article 50(4) first subparagraph deep fakes (image/audio/video) have NO human-review carve-out. Article 50(2) machine-readable marking is a provider duty.

LAYER 2 - PLATFORM TERMS. LinkedIn's stated position is not a legal rule but is enforced harder than one: 'It's ok to use AI to help you write, but your posts and comments need to represent your voice and your perspectives' (VP Laura Lorenzetti, 21 May 2026). LinkedIn also blocks hundreds of thousands of automated comment attempts daily - relevant if any part of your pipeline posts comments. Meta's March 2026 originality rules carry account-level consequences including demonetisation. None of these require disclosure of AI-assisted text; all of them penalise its perceived symptoms.

LAYER 3 - JURISDICTIONAL DIVERGENCE. US FTC rules address deceptive endorsements and testimonials rather than AI authorship, and a July 2026 US federal policy statement moved in a deregulatory direction on AI accuracy suppression - so an EU-based creator with a US audience is governed by the stricter EU rule regardless. Do not import US guidance.

LAYER 4 - GDPR, which is the larger exposure for anyone doing retrieval-grounded drafting. If the corpus the model draws on contains client names, meeting notes or personal data, the legal question is about the CORPUS, not the output. See the sibling item 'RAG-grounded post generation' for the fuller treatment; the gate should include a confidentiality check (do I have the right to publish this?) as a hard stop, and that check is cheap to add and expensive to omit.

NOT LEGAL ADVICE. The definitions above are quoted from public Commission material and a published law-firm analysis; application to any specific publication is a question for a lawyer.

**reversibility and blast radius**

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT: installing the gate is cheap and fully reversible; NOT installing it has an unbounded and largely invisible tail.

BLAST RADIUS OF HAVING THE GATE: near zero. Worst case you lose posting velocity and some engagement in the inspirational-content lane where AI-shaped writing measurably wins. Fully reversible - you can loosen a gate in an afternoon.

BLAST RADIUS OF NOT HAVING IT, escalating:
1. A PRIVATE INAUTHENTICITY FLAG from LinkedIn. Invisible to others, recoverable, and actually the best outcome because at least you find out.
2. REDUCED OUT-OF-NETWORK REACH from a genericness classifier. Account-scoped, persistent, unannounced, and - this is the bad part - UNFALSIFIABLE from your side. You cannot see it, you cannot A/B your way out of it, and normal week-to-week variance will hide it for months. Recovery, where it exists, is slow and unverifiable.
3. ACCOUNT-WIDE NON-RECOMMENDABILITY, Meta-style: a repost / low-originality history makes the whole Page non-recommendable and can pause or block monetisation, with the reach cut applying to that account's ORIGINAL posts too. This is the shape of penalty that makes account-level gating rational.
4. A PUBLISHED FACTUAL ERROR UNDER YOUR OWN NAME. The only item on this list with unbounded reputational cost, the one Gate 1 most directly prevents, and the one most likely to actually happen - models produce confidently specific invented numbers, and in a B2B audience someone will check. Partially recoverable, and a well-handled public correction is itself a strong post - but the recovery costs more than the gate ever would.
5. REGULATORY EXPOSURE. Low probability for personal-brand posting (see the scope argument), bounded at 3% of turnover for an SME, and essentially eliminated by a documented gate.
6. THE ONE WITH NO CARVE-OUT: an AI avatar or cloned voice triggers deep-fake disclosure duties regardless of editorial review. If your pipeline ever generates a synthetic presenter, the gate does not protect you and a separate process is required.

ACCOUNT SUSPENSION is not a realistic outcome of ungated AI-assisted text on any major platform in 2026. It IS a realistic outcome of automated commenting and coordinated inauthentic behaviour, which is a different item (see 'Anti-pattern - inauthentic amplification').

RECOVERABILITY SUMMARY: everything except (4) is a distribution problem that time and better content fix slowly. (4) is the one you cannot undo, and it is the one the gate is best at preventing.

#### practice

**how to apply**

SETUP, once, 2-4 hours.
1. WRITE THE TWO COLUMNS. One page: what the model may produce, what you must supply. Specific enough that a stranger could apply it. Put it in the repo, not in your head.
2. AUDIT EVERY TIMEOUT IN YOUR PUBLISHING PATH. For each tool between draft and publication, answer in writing: what happens if the human never responds? Check Kestra `Pause` (`behavior` defaults to RESUME - change it), Cloudflare Workflows `waitForEvent` (24h default), any scheduler's 'auto-approve after' setting. If the answer is 'it publishes', fix it or remove the tool. Do this BEFORE writing a single checklist item - a gate with a timeout is not a gate.
3. PUT THE APPROVAL OUTSIDE THE AGENT RUNTIME. Drafts land as a pull request; merging is publication. This gives unbounded pause, edit-before-approve, mobile approval, and a commit that is your Article 50 evidence. If a PR is too heavy, the minimum viable version is a drafts folder plus a dated approval log - but keep the approval OUT of the tool that generates.
4. MOUNT REFERENCE CORPORA READ-ONLY. Anything the drafting agent reads from the internet is potentially hostile; writable memory turns one injection into persistent trusted state.
5. NAME THE RESPONSIBLE PERSON AND PUBLISH CONTACT DETAILS. For a solo creator this is a line in your profile. It is also, per the Commission, half of the carve-out.
6. CREATE THE APPROVAL LOG: date, post id, gate results, WHAT THE HUMAN ADDED, approver. One row per post. This is simultaneously the compliance evidence and the source of your gate-health KPIs.

PER POST, 8-15 minutes on top of drafting.
7. WRITE THE FIVE-LINE BRIEF FIRST - claim, evidence, the thing only you know, audience, one action. Before invoking any model. If you cannot write line 3, stop: you do not have a post, you have a topic.
8. DRAFT WITH THE MODEL, grounded in your own corpus where possible.
9. RUN THE CLAIM LEDGER. Every claim, source, class. Source or delete every ABSENT row. No exceptions, and do not let 'it sounds right' substitute for a source.
10. RUN THE SUBSTITUTION AUDIT. Competitor's name, different numbers. If the post survives, it fails Gate 2 - go back to step 7 and supply a real specific.
11. RUN THE HOSTILE EDITOR PASS. Three unsourceable claims, one quotable-against-you sentence, one place a knowledgeable reader objects.
12. EDIT BY HAND, SUBSTANTIVELY. Change a claim, add a hedge, reorder, delete. Surface-only edits do not clear Gate 3. Then classify your own diff and be honest about the answer.
13. FREEZE. No model touches the text again. Not for polish, not for length, not for hashtags.
14. RECORD THE APPROVAL, including the one line that matters: what did I add that the model could not?
15. PUBLISH.

MONTHLY, 20 minutes.
16. COMPUTE THE REJECTION RATE. Below 20%, your gate is decorative - tighten it or admit you have stopped running it.
17. READ YOUR LAST TEN POSTS IN SEQUENCE, looking for shape rather than content: same paragraph count, same opening move, same kind of human input every time. Cross-post uniformity is what pattern detection catches and what you cannot see one post at a time.
18. CHECK FOR A PLATFORM INAUTHENTICITY FLAG.

QUARTERLY, 30 minutes.
19. RE-AUDIT the timeouts (defaults change) and re-read the platform enforcement posture.
20. RE-READ the Commission guidance if it has been amended.

WHAT TO SKIP: buying a detector subscription to check your own posts (you know the answer); building a scoring rubric before you have a rejection-rate habit (you will end up with a rubric and no gate); and any tool marketed as automating human review.

**checklist**

- PASS/FAIL - Did I write the brief BEFORE the model wrote anything? (If the model went first, the gate is already weaker.)
- PASS/FAIL - Does the post contain at least one of: a number I produced with n and method / a dated first-hand incident with a consequence / a named artifact I actually touched / a judgment call with its cost stated / a correction of my own earlier position?
- PASS/FAIL - Substitution audit: if I swap my name for a competitor's and my numbers for different plausible ones, does the post BREAK? (If it survives intact: FAIL.)
- PASS/FAIL - Claim ledger complete, with zero rows left marked ABSENT?
- PASS/FAIL - Can I answer, without a model, 'what would make this post wrong?'
- PASS/FAIL - Can I defend the sharpest likely comment myself, in public, today?
- PASS/FAIL - Was my edit SUBSTANTIVE (changed a claim, added a hedge, reordered, deleted) rather than surface-only? (Spell-check and grammar do not count - this is the Commission's own line.)
- PASS/FAIL - Has NO model touched the text since my review? (A post-review polish pass voids the carve-out and re-adds the tells.)
- PASS/FAIL - Confidentiality: do I have the right to publish every name, number and screenshot in this?
- PASS/FAIL - Is the approval recorded (who, when, what I added), not just performed?
- PASS/FAIL - Timeout check still true: if I never respond, does the pipeline sit and wait rather than publish?
- PASS/FAIL - Shape check across my last ten posts: is the human contribution a different KIND this time, or am I running a template?
- PASS/FAIL - If this post contains synthetic image, audio or video, have I handled the deep-fake disclosure duty SEPARATELY? (The human-review carve-out does not apply there.)
- PASS/FAIL - Monthly: have I rejected at least one finished draft in the last 30 days?

**worked example**

- **real in vault example**:
The vault's own 'Marketing Agent Research' note (content/PROJECTS/AGENTIC-SYSTEMS/Marketing Agent Research.md, 2026-08-25) is a genuine worked example of this gate applied to agent output, and it is worth reading as one. The underlying machine-produced artifact was 31 JSON files and a 1.27 MB, ~14,000-line report across 31 items x 75 fields. The human gate produced a 160-line decision brief and - this is the part that shows the gate ran - it explicitly:
- states that 156 values in the machine output are flagged uncertain and that the raw report is NOT to be read by the implementing agent;
- carries a section headed 'Do rozstrzygniecia przez czlowieka' (to be decided by a human) listing five things the research CANNOT settle, including two named empirical tests the human must run personally (is idle time billed on Managed Agents; does Publer strip C2PA manifests on upload);
- records a CORRECTION to an earlier vault position on Article 50 scope and on the SME penalty basis - i.e. the reviewer changed a claim rather than the wording;
- names eight silent-failure traps, each with its specific mechanism, which is knowledge that came from verification rather than from generation.
Every one of those is a Gate 3 substantive-edit artifact. The note also demonstrates the record requirement: it is a dated commit with an `agent-reviewed` frontmatter field.
- **constructed before after**:
CONSTRUCTED FOR ILLUSTRATION - not a real published post.

MODEL DRAFT (fails the gate):
'Most teams building AI agents make the same mistake: they focus on the model and ignore the workflow. In my experience, the real bottleneck is always human approval. Here are 3 things I have learned about building agent systems that actually ship: 1) Start small. 2) Keep humans in the loop. 3) Measure everything. The teams that get this right move 10x faster.'

GATE RESULTS:
- Gate 1 PROVENANCE: FAIL. '10x faster' is ABSENT - no source, no referent. 'Most teams' is an unsourced universal.
- Gate 2 NON-SUBSTITUTABLE: FAIL. Substitution audit - replace the author with any of four hundred other consultants and every sentence survives verbatim. 'In my experience' is the tell: the phrase claims first-hand knowledge and supplies none.
- Gate 3 SUBSTANTIVE EDIT: not reached.
VERDICT: reject. Not 'improve the wording' - reject, and go back to the brief.

AFTER THE HUMAN SUPPLIES THE MISSING INPUT (type (c), a named artifact with a version and a config value - the most verifiable category):
'We put a human approval step into our publishing pipeline and it did not work for six weeks. Nobody noticed, because it never errored.
Kestra's Pause task defaults to behavior: RESUME. When the timeout expires, the flow continues as if you had approved. Cloudflare Workflows' waitForEvent has a 24-hour default timeout, which sits exactly inside the window you are waiting on a person - and the vendor's own human-in-the-loop example catches the expiry and proceeds with a default action.
So we had a gate that published whenever we were busy. Which is precisely when you want a gate.
We moved approval out of the runtime entirely: drafts land as a pull request, merging is publication. A PR has no timeout. It also lets you EDIT before approving - something no agent permission mode does; defer and always_ask let you say yes or no to what the agent already chose, not change it.
If you have a human-in-the-loop step anywhere, go and check one thing today: what happens if nobody answers? If the answer is that it proceeds, you do not have a gate. You have a delay.'

WHY THIS VERSION CLEARS IT: the claims are checkable against vendor documentation (Gate 1); the substitution audit BREAKS it - swap the author out and the specific configuration knowledge does not transfer (Gate 2); the transferable rule is given away for free; and it carries an admission of a six-week failure, which is the category of input a model will not produce for you because it has nothing to admit.
NOTE THE COST HONESTLY: this version is longer, takes ~40 minutes rather than ~6, and required knowing two specific vendor defaults. That knowledge is the actual asset. The gate does not create it - it refuses to let you publish without it.

#### measurement

**ai search citability**

YES - and this is the item's most under-rated return, because it accrues on a different and far more measurable objective than reach.

WHY THE GATE IS A CITABILITY MECHANISM ALMOST BY ACCIDENT: generative engines need extractable, attributable, self-contained, verifiable statements. Gate 1 (every claim sourced) and Gate 2 (a first-hand specific) produce exactly that object. The claim-ledger step IS the citability step - a claim with its number, sample size and date in the same sentence survives extraction; the same claim with its evidence in an adjacent paragraph does not.

THE SUPPORTING DATA (Semrush, 325,000 prompts / 89,000 cited LinkedIn URLs, data Jan-Feb 2026, published 2026-03-10 - vendor-with-product-to-sell but large-N with disclosed method):
- ~95% of cited LinkedIn content is ORIGINAL rather than reshared. Originality is not a soft preference, it is nearly a precondition.
- 54-64% of cited posts share knowledge or practical advice.
- ~75% of cited authors had posted 5+ times in the previous four weeks - consistency matters, which is the one place the gate's volume cap works against you.
- Median cited post carries only 15-25 reactions. Citability and virality are DIFFERENT objective functions; the gate serves the former much better.
- Sub-500-follower creators are cited comparably to large ones. No follower floor.
- LinkedIn is the #2 most-cited domain across AI answer engines (~11% of responses; ChatGPT Search 14.3%, Google AI Mode 13.5%, Perplexity 5.3%).

THE IMPORTANT CAVEAT, and it changes what you put through the gate: the gate produces citable posts only when the non-substitutable input is a FACT. Category (a) - a number with n and method - and category (c) - a named artifact with a version - are highly citable. Category (b), a personal incident, satisfies the anti-slop gate perfectly and contributes essentially nothing to citation, because an engine cannot extract and attribute a feeling. If citation is an objective for you, weight the input types accordingly rather than defaulting to the anecdote, which is the easiest input to produce.

SECOND-ORDER RISK worth naming: if engines begin discounting social platforms as sources because of AI-slop prevalence - and LinkedIn's 41-81% long-form AI density is exactly the kind of number that would trigger it - then the whole LinkedIn citation channel degrades regardless of your own gate. The gate protects your content; it does not protect the channel.

#### omitted as uncertain

- conflicting evidence
- cost and time to execute
- detectability and disclosure
- effect size and n
- kpis and leading indicators
- measurement feasibility
- prompt artifact link

### Repurposing pipeline

`repurposing-pipeline` · automation L1 · evidence SPLIT · 8 field(s) omitted as uncertain

#### identity

**basics**

Name: Repurposing pipeline. Category: system. DEFINITION: a production system that takes one substantive pillar artifact - a long-form article, a talk, a shipped project, a research pass, a podcast - and DERIVES N posts across M platforms, each re-authored from the underlying evidence for its own surface, rather than excerpted from the pillar and cross-posted. THE DISTINCTION THAT IS THE WHOLE ITEM: DERIVATION versus DUPLICATION. Derivation takes a claim plus the evidence behind it and writes a new, self-contained post for a specific audience on a specific surface. Duplication takes a paragraph and moves it. They look identical on a Kanban board, cost about the same to schedule, and are treated as opposite categories by every major platform's 2026 ranking stack. Meta's own framing captures the line: 'substantially new' analysis or creative reframing still counts as original; low-effort reposts and reaction clips do not. MATURITY: ESTABLISHED as a practice - the 'one pillar, many atoms' model is a decade old. DECAYING as a shortcut. The specific 2026 change is that the penalty for the duplication version stopped being per-post and became per-ACCOUNT: Meta can make an entire Page non-recommendable and demonetised on repost history; Instagram can exclude an account from recommendations for 10+ reposts in 30 days. Which means the cheapest version of this tactic now carries the largest blast radius in the entire research set.

**as of date and volatility**

As of 2026-09-11. Four clocks.
(1) STABLE / years - the underlying logic. Audiences on different surfaces do not overlap completely, most of your own followers do not see any given post, and the second telling of an idea is usually better than the first. None of that is a platform artifact and none of it will rot.
(2) QUARTER-TO-QUARTER - every originality and demotion rule this item has to route around. Meta formalised original-creator rules in March 2026 with account-wide consequences and video fingerprinting that identifies the first uploader; LinkedIn announced reach restriction for AI-appearing content on 2026-05-21 and shipped an AI-slop report on 2026-07-30; Instagram's repost thresholds and third-party-watermark demotion are current-quarter policy. Re-check all of these before relying on any of them.
(3) 6-12 MONTHS - the citation-side numbers. The ~95% original / ~5% reshare split among AI-cited LinkedIn content is a Semrush snapshot from January-February 2026, published 2026-03-10. At least one 2026 analysis reports LinkedIn ARTICLE citations falling 65% in six months, which is exactly the kind of swing that invalidates a share figure. Direction safe, magnitude fragile.
(4) DECAYING FAST / months - the TOOLING edge. Auto-clipping, auto-reframing, auto-captioning and virality scoring were a differentiator in 2023-24 and are table stakes in 2026 at USD 15-29/month. A well-clipped vertical video with burned-in captions is now the floor, not the edge. Any advice premised on the tool being the advantage is already stale.
PRACTICAL RULE: the shape of the pipeline is durable; every specific penalty threshold in it has a three-month half-life. Date-stamp the thresholds separately from the method.

#### mechanism

**how it works**

SIX STAGES. The failure is almost always a collapse of stages 2-4 into 'split and schedule'.

STAGE 1 - SOURCE. The pillar must contain more than one independently defensible claim. This is the gating question and it is quantitative: COUNT THE INDEPENDENT CLAIMS, NOT THE WORDS. A 2,000-word article with one idea yields one post. A 900-word article with five distinct, separately-evidenced claims yields five. Word count is not argument density, and the whole 'turn one blog post into 30 pieces of content' genre rests on confusing the two.

STAGE 2 - DECOMPOSE BY CLAIM, NOT BY SECTION. Extract claims that survive removal from the pillar: each one must be true on its own, surprising to the target audience, and attached to a specific piece of evidence in the source. Section headings are not claims; they are navigation. Decomposing by heading is what produces posts that begin 'Part 3 of my series on...'.

STAGE 3 - RE-ANCHOR TO THE SOURCE, NOT THE PUBLISHED POST. This is the most important mechanical rule in the item and the one nobody states. Every derived output is generated from the ORIGINAL evidence document, never from a previously derived post. Chaining derivations - post 5 written from post 4 - produces generation loss: with each pass, the specifics thin out and the model's own cadence thickens, until the sixth output is pure register with no content. Always re-load the source into context.

STAGE 4 - NATIVE-ISE. Re-author for the surface, which means four separate decisions, not one: FORMAT (is this a text post, a document, a clip, a thread?), LENGTH (the surface's own band), IDIOM (Reddit's register is not LinkedIn's), and SIGNAL (what does this surface actually rank - dwell, sends, completion, comment depth? see 'Social Media Algorithms - Maximizing Reach in 2026'). A post that would read identically on four platforms is native to none of them. Mechanically: always upload natively, never carry a third-party watermark, and re-export rather than re-share.

STAGE 5 - SEQUENCE AND STAGGER. Not a scheduling detail - a detection-avoidance and audience-fatigue measure. Six structurally similar posts in one week is the single clearest pattern a cross-post classifier can see, and it is also how you exhaust the segment of your audience that follows you in two places. Stagger by days, vary the claim TYPE between consecutive posts, and let the surfaces diverge in time as well as in wording.

STAGE 6 - CLOSE THE LOOP. Derived posts are cheap probes. When one outperforms its surface's median by a wide margin, that claim is a candidate for its own pillar - which is how a repurposing pipeline stops being extractive and starts compounding. Instagram's own playbook endorses exactly this shape: repurpose winners into a series within 1-2 days of a breakout.

THE REALISTIC N AND M. N is 4-8 derived posts per genuine pillar, not 30. M is capped by the number of surfaces on which you can actually be native, which for one person is two or three, not the eight your scheduler supports. Vendor promises of 1 video into 30 posts are arithmetic about duplication; the arithmetic is correct and the output is slop.

THE ANTI-PIPELINE, for contrast: SPLIT the pillar into paragraphs, SCHEDULE them, CROSS-POST identically, repeat weekly. This is fast, feels productive, and is precisely the account-level behaviour the 2026 originality stacks are built to catch.

**ranking signal targeted**

TWO ANSWERS, and the honest one first: the pipeline does not primarily target a ranking signal, it targets a COST CURVE. Its purpose is to let you sustain cadence at a substance level you could not sustain by writing everything from scratch. Cadence then feeds signals that other items target.

SIGNALS IT DOES TOUCH, positively:
1. NATIVE-UPLOAD SIGNALS. Directly and mechanically. Facebook native video reportedly earns ~478% more shares than video cross-posted from another app, and cross-posted or watermarked clips forfeit the native-share boost entirely. This is the cleanest, most actionable signal in the item and it costs nothing but a re-export.
2. TOPIC AUTHORITY / SEMANTIC CONSISTENCY. Deriving several posts from one pillar keeps you on one subject, which is what LinkedIn's 360Brew-era topic-authority signal and every engine's author-consistency heuristic reward. This is an underrated benefit: repurposing enforces focus as a side effect.
3. POSTING CONSISTENCY as an AI-citation signal - ~75% of AI-cited LinkedIn authors had posted 5+ times in the previous four weeks (Semrush). The pipeline is the realistic route to that bar.
4. RESHARE-WITH-COMMENTARY weighting on LinkedIn and Substack, which sits above plain reposting in the 2026 hierarchy.

SIGNALS IT TRIPS, negatively - the ones to design around:
5. THE UNORIGINAL-CONTENT / ORIGINALITY CLASSIFIER. Account-scoped on Meta and Instagram; pattern-based across a member's content on LinkedIn.
6. VIDEO FINGERPRINTING. Meta identifies the first uploader. This is deterministic matching, not a probabilistic classifier - you do not get the benefit of the doubt.
7. THIRD-PARTY WATERMARK DETECTION. A visible TikTok or CapCut logo is demoted on Instagram and Facebook and can be outright rejected on TikTok. Trivially detectable, trivially avoidable, and still the most common repurposing mistake.
8. NEAR-DUPLICATE TEXT DETECTION. Cheap for a platform to run and cheap for it to act on.

THE ASYMMETRY WORTH INTERNALISING: the positive signals are modest and probabilistic; the negative signals are mechanical and account-scoped. That asymmetry should shape how much effort goes into native-isation versus into volume.

**why it drives reach**

THREE REAL MECHANISMS, then the reason the same mechanisms make it dangerous.

1. CADENCE. This is the dominant one. Effectiveness thresholds cluster around 2-5 posts per week; the vault's own Marketing Agent Research flagged that 15 posts per month across two brands (~1.8/week/brand) sits BELOW that threshold, citing an analysis of 4.8M posts. Almost nobody can write 2-5 substantive posts per week from scratch. The pipeline is how the cadence bar and the substance bar get satisfied at the same time - and it is the only item in this research that addresses the tension between them rather than ignoring it.

2. AUDIENCE NON-OVERLAP, on two axes. Across platforms, your LinkedIn audience and your X audience are largely different people. Within a platform, any given post reaches a small and effectively random slice of your own followers - so the second telling of an idea is mostly reaching people who never saw the first. Both are real; neither is measurable by you (see measurement_feasibility), which is why this mechanism is easy to over-claim.

3. ITERATION QUALITY. The second articulation of an idea is usually sharper than the first, because you now know which part people argued with. A derived post that incorporates the objection raised in the comments on the pillar is genuinely better content, not a copy - and it is also, by construction, the 'substantially new analysis' that keeps it on the right side of the originality rules.

THE COUNTER-MECHANISM, stated plainly because it is the item's central risk: the pipeline's value proposition is MARGINAL COST REDUCTION, and marginal cost reduction is the engine of slop. Lower the cost per post and volume rises; raise volume without raising substance and you produce exactly the account-level pattern the 2026 classifiers are built to catch. LinkedIn accounted for 62% of all AI-flagged content in the Pangram sample while representing 35% of scanned posts - a feed visibly saturated by pipelines. So the tactic's efficiency is simultaneously its mechanism and its failure mode, and there is no version of this item where that tension is resolved rather than managed.

EMPIRICAL SUPPORT FOR RE-AUTHORING SPECIFICALLY (the one piece of peer-reviewed-adjacent evidence that bears directly on this item): Hu, Jin, Ye, Divakaran and Kumar (arXiv:2505.03769, April 2025) studied exactly this behaviour at scale - Reddit posts sharing YouTube videos, 24.1M Reddit posts across 305K subreddits and 12.6M unique videos. 21% of post titles were minimally modified from the source video title. Rewritten titles were associated with higher engagement: more rewriting (lower title-similarity to the source) correlated with higher post scores at p<0.001. CRITICAL CAVEAT the authors themselves supply: the Spearman correlation is only -0.05, i.e. the effect is real in aggregate and tiny at the level of any individual post. Read that as 'rewrite rather than copy, and do not expect the rewrite alone to carry a post'.

#### ai angle

**ai role**

DRAFT, COMPRESS, VARY, RETRIEVE, TRANSLATE. Not decide, and not chain.

WHAT THE MODEL IS GENUINELY GOOD AT HERE - and this is one of the better AI fits in the research, because the hard input (the pillar) already exists and is grounded:
1. CLAIM EXTRACTION - reading a long document and listing the independently-defensible assertions in it. Reliable, fast, and tedious for a human.
2. FORMAT TRANSLATION - the same claim as a 120-word LinkedIn post, a 6-slide deck outline, a 3-post X thread, a 45-second script. Genuine comparative advantage.
3. COMPRESSION to a surface's length band without losing the load-bearing specific. Note the direction of the risk: compression preferentially drops the evidence, because evidence is the longest part of a claim.
4. VARIANT GENERATION for hooks and openings per surface.
5. DIVERGENCE CHECKING - given six derived drafts, finding the repeated sentences and repeated skeletons. A mechanical task humans are bad at across documents.
6. DRAFT TRANSLATION for a second-language track - with the hard caveat that translation is not localisation (see audience_fit).

WHAT THE MODEL MUST NOT DO:
- DECIDE WHICH CLAIMS DESERVE A POST. That is a judgment about what your specific audience already knows and already believes, and the model has no access to it. Left to the model, you get the claims that are best-formed rather than the claims that are most surprising to your readers - which is how a pipeline produces technically fine posts that land on nobody.
- DERIVE FROM A DERIVED POST. Always re-load the source. Chaining is the generation-loss failure and it is invisible until output four or five.
- SET N. Asked for thirty posts, a model will produce thirty. It has no mechanism for saying 'this pillar contains five ideas'.
- AUTO-PUBLISH ACROSS M SURFACES FROM ONE INPUT. That configuration is the literal behaviour the originality classifiers detect, and several tools offer it as their headline feature.

**automation level**

L1 AI-assisted throughout, with one genuine L2 island and one dangerous L3 temptation.

L1: claim extraction, drafting, compression, variant generation. The human selects and re-authors.
L2 (legitimately autonomous behind guardrails): the VIDEO MECHANICS - clip detection, auto-reframe to vertical, caption burn-in, silence removal, and format conversion. These are deterministic-enough transformations with checkable outputs, and modern tools do them well. Also legitimately L2: the divergence check across derived drafts, and the pre-publish watermark/format lint.
L3, and this is the item's specific hazard: SOURCE IN, MULTI-PLATFORM AUTO-PUBLISH OUT. Several tools offer exactly this and market it as the point of the product. It is the configuration that produces identical text on N surfaces from one input - i.e. the precise pattern that video fingerprinting, near-duplicate detection and account-level originality scoring exist to catch. Nothing credible sits at L3 in 2026 for content that must pass an originality gate, and the tools that claim it are not solving the problem, they are automating the violation.

VENDOR-LABEL WARNING: Opus Clip, Repurpose.io, Castmagic, Munch and Taja are marketed with agent language. Functionally they are L1 clip-and-caption plus an L1 scheduler, with an L2 clipping model inside. That is a useful product and it is not an agent. The judgment steps - which claims, which surfaces, what to add - remain entirely yours, and the tools are designed to make it feel as though they do not.

SAFE DEFAULT CONFIGURATION: automate the mechanics (clipping, reframing, captions, format lint, scheduling of ALREADY-APPROVED posts). Never automate the step between 'source' and 'published on more than one surface'.

**prompt patterns**

Six patterns. Note that four of the six exist to stop the model doing the easy thing.

1. CLAIM EXTRACTION (stage 2).
'Read this document. List every claim that is (a) TRUE AND COMPLETE without the rest of the piece, (b) SURPRISING to [specific audience description], and (c) backed by a SPECIFIC in the source - a number, a name, a version, a date. Output: CLAIM | THE SPECIFIC THAT BACKS IT | WHO WOULD DISAGREE AND WHY. Do not list section headings. Do not list claims you cannot attach a specific to - tell me they exist and stop.'
The (c) condition is the load-bearing one: it forces the evidence to be identified now, while the source is in context, rather than being lost in compression later.

2. SOURCE-ANCHORED RE-AUTHOR (stage 3+4, run once per derived post).
'Here is the full source document. Here is claim #3 and its supporting evidence. Write a LinkedIn post FROM THE EVIDENCE, not from the article's wording. Assume the reader has not read the article and never will. It must be self-contained: no <in my recent piece>, no <as I wrote about>, no <part 2 of>. The specific must appear in the post body.'
Run this separately per claim with the source re-loaded each time. Batching all six into one call is the fastest route to six posts with one voice and one skeleton.

3. DIVERGENCE CHECK (stage 5, run across the whole batch).
'Here are six posts derived from one source. Output: (a) every sentence or distinctive phrase appearing in more than one; (b) the structural skeleton of each, as a list of beats; (c) which two are structurally identical. I need six different thoughts by one person, not six excerpts from one document. Tell me which ones fail that test.'
This is the prompt that catches the cross-post uniformity a classifier would catch.

4. SURFACE IDIOM PASS.
'Rewrite this for [surface]. Constraints: [length band], [format], [the signal this surface ranks - e.g. dwell on LinkedIn, completion on Reels, comment depth on Reddit]. Then tell me what you changed and why. If the honest answer is <almost nothing>, say so - that means this claim does not belong on this surface.'
The escape hatch in the last sentence is deliberate. Not every claim belongs on every surface, and a pipeline without a way to say 'skip this one' will fill every slot.

5. THE ADDITION FORCE (the derivation-versus-duplication gate).
'This post is derived from an existing piece. What does it contain that the source does NOT - a new example, a reframing for this audience, a response to an objection, a second data point? Name it in one sentence. If the answer is nothing, say <this is a duplicate> and stop.'

6. SEQUENCE PLAN.
'Given these six posts, propose a publication order and spacing across two weeks that (a) never places two structurally similar posts adjacent, (b) alternates claim types, and (c) puts the strongest standalone claim first.'

ANTI-PATTERNS, all of which produce excerpts rather than posts: 'turn this article into 10 social posts'; 'make this into a thread'; 'repurpose this for LinkedIn, X and Instagram' in a single call; and any prompt that gives the model the previously derived post instead of the source.

#### evidence

**evidence strength**

SPLIT THREE WAYS, and the strongest evidence is all on the DOWNSIDE.
STRONG / platform-official (direction): that unoriginal and reposted content is demoted, that the penalty is account-scoped on Meta and Instagram, that video fingerprinting identifies the first uploader, and that third-party watermarks cost distribution. These are stated by the platforms in their own transparency material and product announcements. If you take one thing from this entry, take this.
MODERATE / vendor large-N with disclosed method: the ~95% original / ~5% reshare split among AI-cited LinkedIn content (Semrush, 89,000 URLs, 325,000 prompts). Large, methodologically transparent, and produced by a company selling visibility tooling.
MODERATE / peer-reviewed-adjacent preprint: arXiv:2505.03769 on cross-platform title rewriting - very large N (24.1M Reddit posts, 12.6M videos, 86,035 controlled pairs), a genuine controlled design, and an effect the authors themselves describe as tiny at the individual level (Spearman -0.05).
VENDOR-CLAIM / COMPILED: every reach multiplier quoted here - 478% more shares for native video, 40-60% less distribution for reposts, 135% more reach for Reels, 3.2x for original content. These reach this entry through the vault's algorithms compilation, which aggregates marketing-vendor sources that cite each other. Treat DIRECTION as informative and MAGNITUDE as unverified. Do not restate any of them as flat facts.
NON-EXISTENT: any measured effect of running a repurposing pipeline versus not running one. Nobody has measured it and you cannot either.
NET POSITION: the evidence tells you clearly what NOT to do (duplicate, cross-post, watermark, auto-publish to N surfaces) and tells you almost nothing quantitative about what derivation buys. Build for the downside.

**evidence provenance**

PLATFORM-OFFICIAL: Meta Transparency Center on demoted content types; Meta's March 2026 original-creator rules; Instagram's stated repost and watermark rules (largely via Adam Mosseri's public statements); LinkedIn statements of May and July 2026. The highest-confidence material in this item.
INDEPENDENT LARGE-N / ACADEMIC PREPRINT: Hu, Jin, Ye, Divakaran and Kumar, arXiv:2505.03769 (submitted 2025-04-26) - the only genuinely independent large-scale study of cross-platform content adaptation found in this pass. Preprint, not peer-reviewed at time of writing.
VENDOR-WITH-PRODUCT-TO-SELL, LARGE-N, DISCLOSED METHOD: Semrush LinkedIn AI-visibility study (325,000 prompts / 89,000 URLs, Jan-Feb 2026); Pangram (1,002,627 posts, Apr-Jun 2026, opt-in extension sample).
VENDOR-WITH-PRODUCT-TO-SELL, CIRCULARLY CITED: the reach multipliers (478%, 40-60%, 135%, 3.2x). These originate in social-marketing vendor blogs and reach this entry second-hand through the vault's own compilation. Their provenance chains are not individually traceable and several of the 2026 marketing-blog sources in this space are themselves AI-generated. Lowest class present.
VENDOR PRICING, VERIFIED: Opus Clip tier structure and prices, read from the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-09-11.
OWN PRIOR WORK, NOT INDEPENDENT: content/PROJECTS/AGENTIC-SYSTEMS/Marketing Agent Research.md for the existing-toolchain inventory and the cross-language dedup requirement.
VAULT COMPILATION: content/BUSINESS/KNOWLEDGE/INFO/Social Media Algorithms - Maximizing Reach in 2026.md, which is where most per-platform mechanics in this entry come from and which carries its own mixed provenance.
