- VAULT SIBLING: results/Answer-shaped_content_for_AI_citation.json - the citation-side detail behind the 95%/5% split, including the reported 65% six-month collapse in LinkedIn article citations - [sibling research item]
- VAULT SIBLING: results/Multilingual_localization_pipelines.json - why a second-language output is a transcreation problem and not a repurposing output - [sibling research item]
- VAULT SIBLING: results/Carousel_document_architecture.json - the deck as a natural second-order product of a pillar, and the observation that decks do not feature in AI citations - [sibling research item]
- VAULT SIBLING: results/Human-in-the-loop_editorial_protocol.json - the gate each derived post must clear, and the point that the derived post's review is usually weaker than the pillar's - [sibling research item]

#### fit

**platform and format fit**

Cross-referencing 'Social Media Algorithms - Maximizing Reach in 2026' rather than re-deriving ranking mechanics. The per-surface rules below are hard constraints, not preferences.

INSTAGRAM. Native uploads only. No third-party watermarks - a visible TikTok or CapCut logo is demoted in recommendations. Reposts/reshares reportedly get 40-60% less distribution and 10+ reposts in 30 days can exclude the account from recommendations. THE SANCTIONED PATH: Trial Reels (published to non-followers only) to test a derived clip before pushing it to followers, and repurposing breakouts into a series within 1-2 days. Instagram is the platform with the most explicit sanctioned repurposing route AND the sharpest repost penalty.

FACEBOOK. The strictest surface. Video fingerprinting identifies the first uploader; low-effort reposts, stitches and reaction clips without substantially new material are demoted; a repost history can make a whole Page non-recommendable and demonetised, with the reach cut hitting that Page's ORIGINAL posts too. Native uploads reportedly earn ~478% more shares. Never route Facebook through a cross-poster.

TIKTOK. A clip carrying another platform's visible logo is rejected or deprioritised. Re-export clean. Otherwise the most forgiving surface for derived short video.

LINKEDIN. Plain reposts of others' content sit among the weakest formats; reshare-with-commentary is weighted above them. The two highest-value derived formats are the DOCUMENT POST (a deck is a natural second-order product of a pillar - though note the sibling carousel item's finding that decks do NOT feature in AI citations) and the NATIVE ARTICLE at 500-2,000 words, which is where roughly half to two-thirds of LinkedIn's AI citations come from. Keep external links out of the body.

X. Threads derived from a pillar work structurally. The published home-mixer scorer shows demotion aimed at spam and negative downstream reactions rather than at derivation per se.

BLUESKY. Structurally the best surface for driving traffic to a pillar: no link penalty, rich preview cards, and a top referral-traffic source. The counterweight is a strongly anti-AI culture where low-effort content is socially punished rather than algorithmically demoted - which means a visibly pipelined post costs you more here than a reach penalty would.

SUBSTACK NOTES. The platform's own recommended mix explicitly includes original Notes repurposed from your long-form, alongside restacks-with-commentary. Repurposing is endorsed practice here.

PINTEREST. Pin looping - reposting the same image and URL via automation - is demoted. A genuine derived Pin needs a NEW image, a NEW URL and a NEW description. The most mechanically demanding surface for repurposing and usually not worth including in M.

REDDIT. Where repurposing reads worst. Community norms punish marketing-shaped content, many subreddits ban AI-generated posts outright, and AI density there is an order of magnitude below LinkedIn (3% short-form / 13% long-form; 1.7% on replies). Note the irony that the best available study of cross-platform title adaptation is a Reddit-YouTube study: rewriting for the community's norms is exactly what its data says works.

BY FORMAT. HIGHEST-VALUE DERIVED FORMATS: the native long-form article (citation asset), the document post (saves and dwell), the standalone text post carrying one claim plus its evidence. MOST COMMODITISED: the auto-clipped vertical video - everyone has the same tool. WORST: the excerpt, in any format.

**audience fit**

B2B / TECHNICAL: the best fit in the research. Audiences on LinkedIn, X, a newsletter and a blog overlap only partially, the buying cycle is long enough that repetition is an asset rather than an irritation, and the pillar (a talk, a project write-up, a benchmark) is itself the credibility artifact. The specific risk is the opposite of the B2C one: technical audiences notice excerpting immediately and read it as not having anything new to say.

B2C / SHORT VIDEO: the most saturated lane. Auto-clipping is universal and cheap, so the derived clip competes on substance and editing craft, not on existence. The originality penalties also bite hardest here because fingerprinting and watermark detection are most developed for video.

PL VERSUS EN - the most important audience note in this item, and it is a warning against a natural mistake. A second-language version is NOT an output of the repurposing pipeline. Per the sibling 'Multilingual localization pipelines' item, machine translation produces text that is grammatically correct, semantically accurate and unmistakably converted: English word order in Polish sentences, calqued idioms, connective patterns Polish does not use. Native readers detect it instantly, usually cannot articulate why, and respond with silence rather than feedback - so you get no signal that it failed. PL output requires transcreation from the source evidence, which is a stage-3 re-author in Polish, not a stage-4 format pass. Budget it as 1.5-2x a normal derived post, not as a translation step.

ONE CONCRETE ENGINEERING CONSEQUENCE, from Marketing Agent Research: cross-language deduplication requires a `language` dimension in the dedup key. Without it, the pipeline's own duplicate detector will block a legitimate Polish rendering of an English post as a duplicate - a silent failure that removes exactly the content you most wanted.

AUDIENCE OVERLAP IS THE HIDDEN VARIABLE. The more your audiences overlap across surfaces, the less repurposing buys and the more it costs. For a niche technical practitioner with 2,000 followers who largely follow you in two places, M=4 surfaces mostly means showing the same 400 people the same idea four times. You cannot measure this (no platform exposes cross-platform overlap) and you should assume it is higher than you think.

**scales with**

WHAT CAPS IT, in order of how binding it actually is:
1. PILLAR SUPPLY. The pipeline is a MULTIPLIER ON A SCARCE INPUT, and a multiplier on zero is zero. This is the constraint that kills most repurposing systems: the machinery is built, the tools are paid for, and there is nothing worth putting through it. Realistic pillar production for a working consultant is 1-2 per month.
2. ARGUMENT DENSITY OF THE PILLAR. Not length. Count independently-defensible claims. Five claims means five posts, however long the piece is. Attempting eight posts from a three-claim pillar is precisely how derivation degrades into duplication - the extra slots get filled with restatements.
3. SURFACES YOU CAN BE NATIVE ON. M is capped by your ability to write in each surface's idiom and to answer comments there, not by the number of channels your scheduler supports. For one person M is realistically 2-3. The gap between those two numbers is the single biggest source of slop in this item, because the tooling makes M=8 a checkbox.
4. AUDIENCE OVERLAP. Unobservable, and it silently reduces the return as your audience consolidates.
5. TEAM SIZE - and this is one of the very few items in the research where hiring genuinely helps. Stages 4 and 5 (native-isation and sequencing) are delegable craft work. Stage 2 (which claims matter to this audience) is not.

CEILINGS DIFFER BY OBJECTIVE, and sharply:
- VIRALITY: the pipeline raises your number of shots, not your hit rate. More shots on a fat-tailed distribution is genuinely valuable, and this is the honest case for the tactic.
- AI CITATION: hard-capped by originality. A derivation counts as original content and is cited normally; a duplication contributes to the ~5% reshare bucket and is effectively invisible. Note also that citability is follower-independent - sub-500-follower creators are cited comparably to large ones - so the pipeline's citation return does not scale with account size at all.
- TOPIC AUTHORITY: scales well and quietly. Several posts on one subject is what the consistency signals reward.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT: unlike most items here, this one does NOT scale with account size or network position. It scales with how much genuine work you produce, which is the correct incentive and also the reason it feels slower than the tooling promises.

**decay and saturation**

THREE DIFFERENT SHELF LIVES, and conflating them is why 'repurposing is dead' and 'repurposing is essential' are both said by serious people.

THE PRACTICE: does not decay. One body of thinking across several surfaces is a durable model that predates social feeds.

THE TOOLING EDGE: ALREADY GONE. Auto-clip, auto-reframe, auto-caption and virality scoring cost USD 15-29/month and everyone has them. A well-clipped vertical video with burned-in captions is the floor. Any strategy whose advantage is the tool is already commoditised, and the honest timeline on that was roughly 2023-2025.

THE DUPLICATION SHORTCUT: DECAYING FAST AND ASYMMETRICALLY. Cross-posting with watermarks was mildly penalised in 2023 and is now demoted or rejected outright; reposting was a per-post cost and is now an account-level one. The direction of travel is uniform across every platform in the vault's compilation, which is unusual - platforms rarely agree. Expect the boundary to keep moving in the same direction, which means the safety margin you leave today should be larger than the current rules require.

SATURATION, the real one: feeds are saturated with pillar-derived content. LinkedIn showing 62% of all AI-flagged content on 35% of scanned posts is what a feed full of pipelines looks like. The consequence is that derivation quality stops being a differentiator and the differentiator moves BACK UP the chain to the pillar. In a saturated feed, the question stops being 'how well did you atomise it' and becomes 'was it worth atomising'.

WHAT IS APPRECIATING: the pillar itself, and specifically the pillar containing first-hand evidence. It is the one input a pipeline cannot manufacture and the one thing whose scarcity is increasing.

THE SCENARIO THAT WOULD KILL THE ITEM: platform-side semantic (not lexical) duplicate detection across a member's own content. Current detection is near-duplicate text and video fingerprinting, both of which a genuine re-author defeats. Semantic detection would not distinguish derivation from duplication, and would make the whole tactic unusable. No sign of it in 2026; worth watching.

#### risk

**failure modes**

Ten, ordered roughly by frequency. The first two are the ones that quietly define the item.

1. DUPLICATION INSTEAD OF DERIVATION. The definitional failure. It happens by default, because duplication is faster, feels like the same activity, and produces a fuller calendar.
2. GENERATION LOSS. Deriving post 5 from post 4 rather than from the source. Each pass loses specifics and gains model cadence; by the fifth output you have pure register and no content. Invisible while it happens because each individual step looks fine. THE FIX IS MECHANICAL: re-load the source document for every derivation.
3. N SET TOO HIGH. 'One video, thirty posts' forces you to publish claims that were never worth publishing. The correct response to a thin pillar is fewer posts, not more restatements - but no tool in this category will ever tell you that.
4. WATERMARK AND CROSS-POST ARTEFACTS. A visible TikTok logo on a Reel, a vertical crop with the source app's UI in frame, a free-tier vendor watermark. Demoted or rejected, completely avoidable, and still the most common single mistake.
5. CROSS-POST UNIFORMITY. Six derived posts in one week with the same skeleton is the clearest possible signal for a pattern detector, and LinkedIn's stated detection approach looks at exactly this - patterns across a member's content, not individual posts.
6. AUDIENCE OVERLAP FATIGUE. The people who follow you in three places see the same idea three times in five days. You cannot measure this and they will not tell you; they will just stop reading.
7. ACCOUNT-LEVEL PENALTY ACCUMULATION. The one with real blast radius. A scheduler configured to auto-cross-post accrues a repost history faster than you notice, and Meta's remedy is Page-wide non-recommendability plus demonetisation. By the time the reach drop is visible, the history exists.
8. THE SCHEDULER ILLUSION. A queue full of scheduled derived posts feels like a working system. It is actually a standing commitment to publish things you have not re-read, on days when the context may have changed.
9. ORPHANED EVIDENCE. The claim travels to the derived post and the number that backed it stays in the pillar, because compression drops the longest element first. The result is a post that asserts confidently and proves nothing - which is indistinguishable from generated content and is scored accordingly.
10. THE DEAD PILLAR. The pipeline keeps emitting from a source whose claims have gone stale. Especially dangerous for platform-mechanics content, where a six-month-old number is actively wrong.

FAILURE SIGNATURE: derived posts performing consistently below the pillar AND below your surface median, with comments that are generic rather than specific. That pattern means the evidence is not travelling.

**ai slop risk**

HIGH - structurally, not incidentally. This is among the two or three highest slop-risk items in the research, and the reason is economic rather than technical: the pipeline's entire value proposition is marginal cost reduction, and marginal cost reduction is the mechanism that produces slop. Every efficiency gain here is also a quality risk, and there is no configuration where that is not true.

THE TELLS, in rough order of reliability:
1. CROSS-POST SKELETON REPETITION. Six posts in one week with the same beat structure - hook, three short lines, turn, one-line payoff, question. This is the most reliable tell and the only one visible from outside your account.
2. CONTEXT-DEPENDENT OPENINGS. 'In my recent article...', 'Part 3 of...', 'As I mentioned last week...'. These prove the post was cut from something rather than written for the reader in front of it.
3. ASSERTION WITHOUT EVIDENCE. The claim arrived; the number stayed behind in the pillar. The single most diagnostic in-post tell.
4. REPEATED SENTENCES across outputs - the literal fingerprint of duplication and the easiest thing for both a reader and a classifier to catch.
5. UNIFORM LENGTH. Human output is ragged; pipeline output is suspiciously even, because the length came from a parameter.
6. PLATFORM-AGNOSTIC PHRASING. A post that would read identically on LinkedIn, X and Threads is native to none of them, and that neutrality is itself a signature.
7. THE HASHTAG BLOCK CARRIED ACROSS SURFACES unchanged - a small tell that reliably indicates a cross-poster rather than a human.

WHAT ACTUALLY DEFEATS IT - only one thing, and it is not a prompt: THE PER-POST ADDITION. Something in each derived post that is not in the pillar. A second example, a reframe for that surface's audience, a response to an objection raised in the comments on the previous post, a caveat you have since thought of. This is also, not coincidentally, exactly what Meta describes as 'substantially new' analysis or creative reframing. The addition gate is the item's single load-bearing quality control, and everything else here is hygiene.

**human input required**

TWO LEVELS, and the second is the one people skip.

LEVEL 1 - THE PILLAR MUST CLEAR THE EDITORIAL GATE. Everything in the sibling item 'Human-in-the-loop editorial protocol' applies to the source: a first-hand number with n and method, a dated incident with a consequence, a named artifact you actually touched, a judgment call with its cost, or a correction of your own earlier position. A pipeline run on a pillar with no non-substitutable content produces N slop posts instead of one, which is the cheapest way to turn a quality problem into an account-level problem.

LEVEL 2 - PER DERIVED POST, three non-substitutable contributions:
(a) THE CLAIM SELECTION. Deciding which of the pillar's claims deserves its own post is a judgment about what your specific audience already knows, already believes, and would argue with. The model cannot make it - it has no model of your readers - and left to itself it will select the best-FORMED claims rather than the most SURPRISING ones. This is why pipelined content is so often technically fine and lands on nobody.
(b) THE EVIDENCE THAT TRAVELS. Each derived post must carry a specific from the source into the post body - the number with its sample size, the version string, the date, the name. If the specific stays in the pillar, you have published an assertion. This is the single most checkable requirement in the item and the one compression most reliably breaks.
(c) THE ADDITION - something in the derived post that is NOT in the pillar. A new example, a reframing for this surface's audience, a reply to an objection, a caveat you have since formed. This is the derivation/duplication gate, it maps directly onto Meta's 'substantially new analysis or creative reframing', and it is the only one of the three that a determined person can fake by writing a different intro - so check it honestly.

PLUS, unconditionally: READ EACH DERIVED POST AS A STANDALONE ARTIFACT, cold, as if you had never seen the pillar. Half of the failures in this item are visible in ten seconds of that reading and invisible in any amount of reviewing-in-context.

A WARNING WORTH STATING: the derived post's human review is almost always weaker than the pillar's, because it feels like a formality - the thinking was already done. That is exactly backwards from a compliance standpoint (the Article 50 carve-out attaches per publication, not per pillar) and from a quality standpoint (the derived post is the one most readers will actually see).

**detectability and disclosure**

THE IMPORTANT REFRAME: in this item, DUPLICATION IS FAR MORE DETECTABLE THAN AI AUTHORSHIP. The AI-text question that dominates the rest of this research is secondary here; the platforms have deterministic tools for the thing that actually goes wrong.

DETECTION THAT IS DETERMINISTIC, NOT PROBABILISTIC:
- VIDEO FINGERPRINTING. Meta identifies the first uploader of a video. This is matching, not classification - there is no false-positive argument to make and no benefit of the doubt.
- WATERMARK DETECTION. A visible third-party logo is trivially found. Demotion on Instagram and Facebook; rejection or deprioritisation on TikTok.
- NEAR-DUPLICATE TEXT MATCHING. Cheap to run at platform scale, and the version of the pipeline that pastes the same paragraph onto four surfaces is exactly what it finds.
PROBABILISTIC, AND THE ONE A GENUINE RE-AUTHOR DEFEATS: cross-post pattern and genericness classification - LinkedIn's stated approach of looking at patterns across a member's content. A derivation with distinct evidence, structure and framing per surface does not present that pattern. A duplication does.

THE PROVENANCE POINT SPECIFIC TO THIS ITEM: C2PA content credentials are STRIPPED when a file is re-downloaded from Instagram. Provenance therefore does NOT survive a repurposing chain. If any part of your visual pipeline depends on C2PA credentials persisting - for AI-labelling, for attribution, for anything - verify it end to end on your own pipeline rather than assuming, because the default behaviour is loss. Marketing Agent Research flags the untested question of whether Publer strips C2PA manifests on upload as an empirical test still owed.

DISCLOSURE: repurposing triggers no disclosure duty of its own. The EU AI Act analysis is inherited from the drafting step and is set out in the sibling 'Human-in-the-loop editorial protocol' item. ONE NON-OBVIOUS CONSEQUENCE: the Article 50(4) carve-out attaches PER PUBLICATION. If the pillar received substantive human review and the six derived posts received a glance, the carve-out is strong for the pillar and weak for the six things most people will actually read. Platform labels are a non-issue for text; if a derived output is a synthetic-media clip (AI avatar, cloned voice), the deep-fake duties apply and have no human-review carve-out.

**policy and legal**

ASSUMING A POLAND/EU-BASED CREATOR. The binding layer here is platform terms, not statute - which is the reverse of most items in this research.

LAYER 1 - PLATFORM RULES, the ones with teeth:
- META (March 2026): rules 'rewarding original creators'. Video fingerprinting identifies the first uploader. Low-effort reposts, stitches and reaction clips without substantially new material are demoted. A Page with a repost history can be made NON-RECOMMENDABLE and DEMONETISED account-wide, with the reach cut applying to its original posts too. The carve-out is 'substantially new' analysis or creative reframing, which is undefined.
- INSTAGRAM: reposts/reshares reportedly lose 40-60% of distribution; 10+ reposts in 30 days can exclude the account from recommendations; third-party watermarks are demoted.
- TIKTOK: clips carrying another platform's visible logo are rejected or deprioritised.
- PINTEREST: pin looping via automation is demoted.
- LINKEDIN: no explicit repurposing rule, but plain reposts are among the weakest formats and the May/July 2026 AI-content enforcement applies to whatever your pipeline emits.
None of these are laws and all of them are enforced automatically, immediately and without appeal - which in practice makes them the operative regulation.

LAYER 2 - COPYRIGHT AND CONSENT, the layer that actually creates legal risk:
- Repurposing YOUR OWN material is clean.
- Clipping a podcast, webinar or panel with a GUEST requires the guest's permission - and permission to appear on the original is not permission to appear in a 45-second clip on a platform they did not agree to. Get this in writing at recording time; retrofitting it is painful.
- Screenshots, quotes and charts from third parties carried into derived posts multiply the exposure by N. One borderline use in a pillar becomes six borderline uses.
- Music and stock footage licences are frequently per-platform. A clip licensed for YouTube is not automatically licensed for TikTok.

LAYER 3 - GDPR AND CONFIDENTIALITY, and the important structural point: the confidentiality check must run PER OUTPUT, not once per pillar. Every derived post re-publishes whatever client data it carries, to a new audience, on a new surface, often in a more decontextualised form. A detail that was safe inside 2,000 words of framing can be re-identifying as a standalone 100-word post. NDAs and client contracts apply per publication.

LAYER 4 - EU AI ACT: inherited from the drafting step, no new duty created by derivation. See the sibling HITL item, and note the per-publication point in detectability_and_disclosure.

NOT LEGAL ADVICE.

**reversibility and blast radius**

THE HIGHEST STRUCTURAL BLAST RADIUS IN THIS RESEARCH apart from inauthentic amplification - and unlike most items here, the mechanism is documented rather than inferred.

WORST CASE, and it is concrete: Meta's Page-wide non-recommendability plus demonetisation for a repost history. Not the offending clip - the whole account, including its original posts. Instagram's parallel is exclusion from recommendations for 10+ reposts in 30 days. These are account-scoped, automatic, and not announced to you.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN IT LOOKS: the penalty attaches to a HISTORY, and a misconfigured scheduler accumulates history fast. An auto-cross-post setup can cross the Instagram threshold in a month without a single deliberate decision. By the time the reach drop is large enough to notice against normal variance, the qualifying history already exists. This is the one place in the research where a checkbox in a tool can cost you an account's distribution.

RECOVERABILITY: poorly documented and slow. Platforms do not publish how a repost history ages out, whether it does, or what remediation looks like. Assume months, assume no notification, and assume you cannot verify recovery - which means prevention is the only available strategy.

OTHER OUTCOMES, lower:
- Individual post demotion for a watermark or cross-post. Per-post, trivially preventable, no lasting cost.
- Audience attrition from overlap fatigue. Slow, silent, and genuinely reversible by slowing down.
- Reputational cost of visible excerpting: modest but real in technical audiences, where it reads as having nothing new.
- Copyright or consent complaint over a clipped guest: low probability, real cost, and the one that can involve actual lawyers.

SUSPENSION is not a realistic outcome of ordinary repurposing. Demonetisation and non-recommendability are.

THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR SYSTEM DESIGN: because the penalty is account-level and the detection is deterministic, this is one of the few items where you should build the guardrail BEFORE the capability. Audit the cross-post settings, kill auto-publish, and add a watermark/format lint to the pipeline before you derive your first batch - not after.

#### practice

**how to apply**

SETUP, once, 2-3 hours.
1. AUDIT AND DISABLE AUTO-CROSS-POST everywhere. Every scheduler, every 'connect your accounts' integration, every tool with a 'publish to all' toggle. This is the single highest-value action in the item and it takes twenty minutes. Do it before anything else.
2. WRITE surface-specs.yaml: for each surface you will actually use, its length band, its formats, the signal it ranks, and its hard rules (native upload only; no third-party watermark; link policy). Pull these from the vault's algorithms note so they live in one place and can be updated once.
3. SET M HONESTLY. Two or three surfaces you can be native on and answer comments on. Not eight.
4. CREATE pillar-ledger.csv: pillar, date, claims extracted, posts derived, surfaces, which derived post outperformed. This is what makes stage 6 a loop rather than an intention.

PER PILLAR.
5. CHECK THE PILLAR CLEARS THE EDITORIAL GATE (sibling item). If it carries no non-substitutable content, do not run the pipeline - you would be multiplying a quality problem into an account-level one.
6. EXTRACT CLAIMS with prompt pattern 1. Count them. THE NUMBER OF CLAIMS IS YOUR N. Do not round up.
7. ASSIGN CLAIMS TO SURFACES deliberately. Not every claim goes everywhere. A claim with a number belongs where numbers are read; a claim with a story belongs where stories are read. Expect to drop claims that fit nowhere.
8. RE-AUTHOR EACH ONE SEPARATELY with prompt pattern 2, RE-LOADING THE SOURCE EVERY TIME. One call per derived post. Batching is the generation-loss failure.
9. CARRY THE EVIDENCE. Check explicitly that each derived post contains the specific - the number, the version, the date, the name - in its body. This is the check compression most reliably breaks.
10. ADD SOMETHING. Per post, name in one sentence what is here that was not in the pillar. If you cannot, cut the post.
11. RUN THE DIVERGENCE CHECK (pattern 3) across the whole batch. Fix or cut anything structurally identical to something else in the batch.
12. NATIVE-ISE MECHANICALLY: native upload, clean re-export with no third-party watermark, correct aspect ratio, platform-appropriate captions and alt text, link policy per surface.
13. READ EACH POST COLD as a standalone artifact. This is not the same as reviewing it; it is reading it as a stranger.
14. SEQUENCE AND STAGGER (pattern 6). Never two structurally similar posts adjacent. Spread across days, not hours.
15. PUBLISH ONE SURFACE AT A TIME, not simultaneously.

AFTER.
16. RECORD which derived post outperformed its surface's median, and by how much.
17. PROMOTE WINNERS: a derived post that strongly outperforms is a candidate for its own pillar. This is the loop that makes the pipeline compound instead of deplete.
18. MONTHLY: check the derivation ratio (posts per pillar). Above ~12, you are duplicating. Check for any accumulating repost history on Meta surfaces.

WHAT TO SKIP: the eighth surface; the free tier of any clipping tool (the watermark defeats the purpose); 'repurpose this for all platforms' as a single prompt; and any tool whose headline feature is publishing to N surfaces from one input.

**checklist**

- PASS/FAIL - Does the pillar itself clear the editorial gate (a real number, incident, artifact, judgment call or correction)? If not, do not run the pipeline at all.
- PASS/FAIL - Is N equal to the number of INDEPENDENT CLAIMS in the pillar, rather than a target I chose in advance?
- PASS/FAIL - Was every derived post written from the SOURCE document, not from another derived post?
- PASS/FAIL - Does each derived post carry a SPECIFIC from the source - a number, a version, a date, a name - in its body?
- PASS/FAIL - Can I name, in one sentence per post, what is in it that was NOT in the pillar? (If not: it is a duplicate. Cut it.)
- PASS/FAIL - Is each post self-contained? No 'in my recent piece', no 'part 2 of', no assumed context.
- PASS/FAIL - Divergence check run: no sentence and no skeleton repeated across the batch?
- PASS/FAIL - Native upload, clean re-export, NO third-party watermark, correct aspect ratio for each surface?
- PASS/FAIL - Auto-cross-post is disabled and each surface is being published to deliberately?
- PASS/FAIL - Sequencing: no two structurally similar posts adjacent, spread across days?
- PASS/FAIL - Link policy respected per surface (out of the body where penalised; Bluesky is the surface that does not penalise links)?
- PASS/FAIL - Confidentiality re-checked FOR THIS POST, not just for the pillar? (A detail safe in 2,000 words can be re-identifying in 100.)
- PASS/FAIL - If a guest or third party appears in a clip, do I have permission for THIS clip on THIS platform?
- PASS/FAIL - Have I read this post cold, as a stranger who will never see the pillar?
- PASS/FAIL - Monthly: is my derivation ratio under ~12 posts per pillar, and is there no accumulating repost history on Meta surfaces?

#### measurement

**kpis and leading indicators**

PIPELINE-HEALTH METRICS (primary - you own these and they are the early warning):
1. DERIVATION RATIO - published posts per pillar. Target 4-8. Above ~12 you are duplicating, whatever you call it. The most diagnostic single number in the item.
2. EVIDENCE-CARRY RATE - share of derived posts containing a specific from the source in the post body. Target 100%. Anything less means compression is eating your evidence.
3. ADDITION RATE - share of derived posts for which you can name, in one sentence, what is in them that was not in the pillar. Target 100%.
4. SKELETON DIVERSITY - number of distinct structural shapes across the last ten posts. A falling number is a template forming, and it is what a cross-post classifier sees.
5. SURFACE COUNT ACTUALLY MAINTAINED versus surfaces connected. A growing gap means the pipeline is publishing where you are not present.
6. PROMOTION RATE - derived posts elevated into their own pillars. Zero means the loop is open and the pipeline is purely extractive.

OUTCOME METRICS, per surface and against THAT SURFACE'S own median (never against the pillar, and never pooled across platforms):
- Impressions per follower, engagement rate per impression, saves and sends where exposed.
- Pillar traffic or subscriptions attributable to derived posts, where a link exists.
- Citation of the PILLAR by AI engines - the pipeline's real long-term return and the slowest to appear.

LEADING INDICATORS, in order of usefulness:
- Comments on a derived post that reference something NOT in the pillar. This is direct evidence the addition landed and is the best qualitative signal available.
- A derived post outperforming its surface median by a wide margin - promote that claim to a pillar.
- The inverse warning sign: derived posts clustering consistently BELOW your surface median while the pillar performs normally. That pattern means the evidence is not travelling, and it appears weeks before any reach penalty would.

WHAT NOT TO TRACK: total posts published (the metric that produces the failure mode); pooled cross-platform engagement (meaningless - the medians differ by an order of magnitude); and any comparison of a derived post to the pillar, which will always flatter the pillar and tells you nothing.

#### omitted as uncertain

- ai search citability
- conflicting evidence
- cost and time to execute
- effect size and n
- measurement feasibility
- prompt artifact link
- tool examples
- worked example

### Voice corpus and style transfer

`voice-corpus-style-transfer` · automation L2 · evidence SPLIT · 13 field(s) omitted as uncertain

#### identity

**basics**

- **name**: Voice corpus and style transfer
- **category**: system
- **definition**: Assembling your own published writing into a versioned reference corpus, using it to condition generation (style spec / few-shot exemplars / per-author adapter), and scoring drafts against it with a non-LLM stylometric metric so 'does this sound like me' becomes a number rather than an impression.
- **maturity**: established as measurement, emerging-and-capped as generation. The stylometry half rests on a 2002 method with peer-reviewed sample-size guidance and multiple independent implementations. The generation half has a hard, measured ceiling that no 2026 inference-time technique clears.
- **the finding that should reset expectations**: PersonalBench (arXiv 2608.19746): across 50 authors and 1,000 generations, every personalization method landed at LUAR similarity 0.484-0.508 to the real author — below the 0.626 cross-author HUMAN floor. Inference-time personalization does not reach even the level of similarity between two DIFFERENT humans. The spread between methods was 0.024. Your prompt engineering is not the variable.

#### mechanism

**how it works**

- **three layers that get confused**: VOICE SPECIFICATION (what you tell the model), VOICE SCORING (how you check the output), and VOICE ARCHITECTURE (whether the model was modified at all). Most 'brand voice' tooling collapses all three into a prompt. Keeping them separate is the whole design, because the specification layer is cheap and weak, the scoring layer is cheap and strong, and the architecture layer is expensive and the only one with evidence of beating prompting.
- **layer 1 corpus**:
  - The corpus is your published writing, in full text, tagged by (author/brand, language, register). It is the reference against which everything is measured and the only genuinely proprietary component.
  - Eder's minimum-sample study puts reliable Delta attribution at 2,500-5,000 words, with 5,000 stated explicitly for Polish. At LinkedIn post lengths that is roughly 15 posts as an absolute FLOOR — and Eder's figure assumes a single contiguous sample, whereas pooled short posts across varied topics are noisier than that.
  - Practical target: 25-30 posts per (brand, language) cell before the number is trustworthy; 50-200 is the honest working band. Two brands × two languages = four cells = 100-120 exemplar posts for full coverage. The cells cannot share a corpus if the registers genuinely differ — which is the reason a voice gate exists at all.
- **layer 2 specification three competing methods**:
  - **style spec**: A written rulebook — sentence-length distribution, vocabulary preferences, structural habits, banned constructions, characteristic moves. Cheapest, most legible, model-portable, and reviewable by a human. Captures the explicit half of a voice and misses the tacit half entirely.
  - **few shot exemplars**: Paste 5-15 real posts into the prompt. Captures rhythm and tacit patterning that a spec cannot articulate. Costs tokens on every call, and PersonalBench's finding is that this and every other inference-time method land in the same statistically indistinguishable band.
  - **fine tune or adapter**: Modify the model. AuthorMix (arXiv 2603.23069) is the current reference point: per-author LoRA adapters for high-resource authors, then layer-wise ADAPTER MIXING to reach a new target author from only a handful of examples. It reports beating SoTA style-transfer baselines and GPT-5.1 on low-resource targets while improving meaning preservation. This is the only family with published evidence of beating prompting — and it costs a per-author artifact that must be versioned and retrained as the voice evolves.
  - **the honest ranking**: For a solo operator at 10-20 posts a month: style spec + few-shot exemplars, because they are nearly free and the literature says the expensive option's advantage is real but modest relative to its operational cost. Revisit adapters only when the corpus passes several hundred posts AND the score plateaus below threshold despite prompt work.
- **layer 3 scoring**:
  - **the rule**: The voice score must NOT come from an LLM judge. An LLM asked 'does this sound like the author' is scoring its own output family with its own priors, and semantic embeddings are worse — the semantic-embedding class (text-embedding-3-large and relatives) measures TOPIC, not style, and looks rigorous while doing it.
  - **primary metric**: Burrows's Delta via faststylometry. Z-scored relative frequencies of the top-N most frequent words, Manhattan distance to the reference corpus. CPU, milliseconds, zero cost, no model. faststylometry exposes predict_proba(), so the output is a calibrated probability ('this batch has a 12% chance of being by this author') rather than an arbitrary distance.
  - **secondary metric**: mStyleDistance (arXiv 2502.15168) — multilingual contrastive style embeddings, nine languages, MIT-licensed, XLM-RoBERTa-base, ~1.1 GB, CPU-runnable. Content-independent by construction, which is exactly what semantic embeddings are not. Its English predecessor StyleDistance (NAACL 2025) trains on synthetic near-exact paraphrases across 40 style features.
  - **authorship verification metric**: LUAR — authorship representations trained on large-scale Reddit data (the Million User Dataset), used in PersonalBench as the reference verifier. It is what the ceiling result is measured with, so it is the right instrument for asking 'how far off am I' even though Delta is the better daily gate.
- **the single most important operational finding**: NEVER SCORE A SINGLE POST. PersonalBench measures LUAR's single-post AUC at 0.76 against 0.96 at five posts. A per-post gate is wrong roughly a quarter of the time, which at 15 posts a month means several false rejections monthly and a gate that gets switched off within a quarter. Score rolling batches of five or more drafts from the same (brand, language) cell. This is a workflow change — batch the drafting — not an engineering one, and it is the part most likely to be resisted.

#### ai angle

**ai role**

- **draft**: Generate against the style spec plus few-shot exemplars. Expect help at the margin and not authorship — PersonalBench's 0.024 spread across methods means the conditioning technique is nearly irrelevant to how close you land.
- **score**: NOT the model's job. This is the one place in the pipeline where the number must come from arithmetic, not from a judge. Delta primary, mStyleDistance as a benchmarked second opinion.
- **critique**: Genuinely useful and under-used: ask a model to name the SPECIFIC divergences ('you never use rhetorical questions; this draft has three'), given the style spec as input. Diagnostic output, not a score.
- **retrieve**: Pull the closest exemplars from the corpus for the topic at hand rather than always passing the same fifteen. Cheap improvement to conditioning and it keeps the prompt smaller.
- **vary**: Generate the five drafts the batch-scoring requirement needs. This turns a constraint into a use — you need five anyway, so generate five genuinely different angles rather than five paraphrases.
- **the thing to refuse**: An LLM-produced voice score. It looks rigorous, it is cheap, it correlates with topic rather than style, and it will pass exactly the generic drafts the gate exists to catch.

**automation level**

- **level**: L2 — autonomous with guardrails, and the guardrail is the point.
- **detail**: The gate makes the drafting step safe enough to leave unattended, because a draft failing the voice floor never reaches the human queue. Scoring, threshold comparison and CI exit codes are fully mechanical. What stays human is (a) the corpus curation decision — what counts as canonical you — and (b) publication itself.
- **why it must not become L3**: Given that no inference-time method reaches even the similarity between two different humans, a passing voice score is emphatically NOT evidence that a post is publishable unread. The temptation this item creates is precisely to treat a good number as permission to skip the human — which is both the quality failure and the loss of the Art. 50(4) editorial-responsibility posture. Keep it a filter, never a licence.
- **vendor label warning**: Every commercial 'brand voice' product is L1 dressed as L2, and it measures a different thing. Across Acrolinx/Markup AI, Textmetrics, Grammarly and Writer.com, 'brand voice' means conformance to a STYLE GUIDE, not similarity to a CORPUS. Nobody sells 'how close is this to my 500 exemplar posts', in any language. For a personal brand that is the only question that matters.

**prompt patterns**

- **patterns**:
  - **name**: Style-spec extraction from the corpus | **shape**: Here are 30 of my published posts. Produce a style specification with SIX sections: (1) sentence-length distribution with actual numbers from these posts; (2) five constructions I use repeatedly, quoted verbatim from the corpus with the post they came from; (3) five constructions I never use — check, do not guess; (4) how I open and how I close, with three examples of each; (5) my characteristic MOVE — the structural thing I do that another writer on this topic would not; (6) vocabulary I avoid, quoted as evidence of absence. Every claim must be backed by a quote or a count from the corpus. Where you cannot evidence a claim, omit it. | **why**: The evidence requirement is what separates a real spec from a horoscope. Unconstrained, a model produces 'conversational yet authoritative' for everyone. Forcing a quote or a count per claim makes the spec falsifiable and makes the omissions visible.
  - **name**: Retrieval-conditioned drafting | **shape**: Reference posts (closest five from my corpus on this topic, full text): <exemplars>. Style spec: <spec>. Write a post about <topic>. Constraints: use my opening pattern, not a generic hook; include the specific number/name/date I gave you; do not introduce any construction absent from the reference posts. Produce FIVE genuinely different angles, not five paraphrases. | **why**: Retrieval keeps the exemplars relevant instead of static, and the five-draft requirement exists because the scoring gate needs a batch of at least five. One instruction satisfies both the conditioning and the measurement design.
  - **name**: Divergence diagnosis, not scoring | **shape**: Here is my style spec, derived from my corpus. Here is a draft. List every place the draft violates the spec, quoting the draft text and naming the rule it breaks. Do not rate the draft. Do not say whether it sounds like me. List violations only, or state NONE. | **why**: The 'do not rate' clause is load-bearing. The moment a model gives a number it has become a judge, and the whole architecture here exists to keep judging out of the loop. Violations are checkable; a score is not.
  - **name**: Impostor generation for threshold calibration | **shape**: Here are the topics of my last 30 posts. Write a competent LinkedIn post on each topic, in a professional but generic B2B voice, with no attempt to imitate any specific author. These will be used as negative examples for a stylometric classifier. | **why**: You cannot set a threshold without negatives, and no published benchmark measures whether a metric can tell YOUR writing from a competent imitation of it. Impostors are free and unlimited to generate, which turns threshold calibration from a guess into an ROC curve. 30-50 genuine batches against 30-50 impostor batches per cell gives a usable curve; below that the cut-off is guesswork.
  - **name**: Corpus curation triage | **shape**: For each of these posts of mine, answer: is it (a) canonical voice, (b) off-register (a format experiment, a reshare comment, a crisis post), or (c) not my writing (heavily edited, ghostwritten, translated). Justify in one clause. Return three lists. | **why**: A corpus that includes your off-register writing has a wider variance and a mushier centroid, and the gate then accepts too much. But a corpus curated too narrowly is worse — see failure_modes. The triage should EXCLUDE (c), flag (b), and keep deliberate variety within (a).

**tool examples**

- **scoring primary**: faststylometry — Burrows's Delta in Python, CPU, milliseconds, predict_proba() for calibrated output. CRITICAL: override the default tok_match_pattern r'^[a-z][a-z]+$', which silently discards every Polish diacritic-bearing word and returns confident numbers from a mutilated vocabulary. Add a startup assertion that fails loudly if the pattern is default and the corpus language is not English.
- **scoring reference implementation**: stylo (R) — Eder and Rybicki, Jagiellonian University. The canonical Delta implementation and, incidentally, Polish computational-stylistics work, which is part of why the method is unusually well characterised on Polish.
- **embeddings**: StyleDistance/mstyledistance on Hugging Face — MIT, XLM-RoBERTa-base, ~1.1 GB, CPU-runnable for a few dozen documents. English predecessor: StyleDistance (NAACL 2025), trained on synthetic near-exact paraphrases across 40 style features.
- **authorship verification**: LUAR — the authorship-representation model used as the reference verifier in PersonalBench. Use it to measure the gap, not as the daily gate.
- **adapters if you ever go there**: AuthorMix (arXiv 2603.23069) — per-author LoRA plus layer-wise adapter mixing; reports beating SoTA baselines and GPT-5.1 on low-resource targets. The only published family with evidence of beating prompting.
- **external benchmark**: PAN@CLEF 2018 authorship attribution — English, French, Italian, Polish, Spanish. A free external calibration set, and the source of a sobering number: Polish was the HARDEST of the five, best macro-F1 0.556, with the task overview stating 'The most difficult cases appear to be the Polish ones.'
- **commercial comparison for completeness**: Markup AI (formerly Acrolinx) — the Acrolinx Score out of 100 with a discrete TONE goal score, a public API and a GitHub Action for branch protection; $249/mo Starter, $999/mo Business. Caveats that disqualify it here: NO Polish anywhere in its language matrix or its API spec; Tone supported on only 6 of 10 language rows; numeric scoring gated behind a PER-ORGANISATION FEATURE FLAG, so the subscription does not reliably buy the score. Textmetrics is EN/NL/DE/FR; Grammarly is Enterprise-gated with a dead Editor SDK; Writer.com has no scoring endpoints.
- **explicitly reject**: OpenAI's graders endpoint as a fallback. score_model is an LLM judge and text-embedding-3-large is exactly the semantic-embedding class that fails on style — the most dangerous option available, because it looks rigorous while measuring topic.

**evidence provenance**

Patel, Zhu, Qiu, Horvitz, Apidianaki, McKeown, Callison-Burch — 'StyleDistance', NAACL 2025. Khan, Fleming, Schofield, Bishop, Andrews — 'A Deep Metric Learning Approach to Account Linking', NAACL 2021 (the LUAR lineage). Burrows, J. — 'Delta: a measure of stylistic difference', 2002.

**sources**

#### fit

**platform and format fit**

- **cross reference**: Ranking mechanics per platform are in content/BUSINESS/KNOWLEDGE/INFO/Social Media Algorithms — Maximizing Reach in 2026.md. Only the voice layer is covered here.
- **platform agnostic by construction**: This scores TEXT, so it applies identically to a LinkedIn post, a newsletter, a blog or a conference abstract. That generality matters more than usual: the voice being protected is a PERSON'S, not a channel's, and the same reference corpus should govern everywhere that person writes. Do not build per-platform voice corpora; build per-(person, language, register) corpora.
- **linkedin**: Why the item exists rather than being a nicety. The platform's 2026 suppression of AI-classified content in out-of-network recommendations means generic copy is structurally throttled exactly where the incremental reach lives. One platform-specific caution: LinkedIn rewards a fairly narrow register, so optimising hard against a personal corpus can pull drafts away from what performs there. Floor, not objective.
- **reddit and bluesky**: Highest stakes for voice and lowest tolerance for its absence. Enforcement is human — readers, mods, block lists — and a post that reads as generic is punished socially rather than algorithmically. A voice gate helps; a voice gate calibrated on your LinkedIn corpus actively hurts, because the register is different. Separate cell or do not use it.
- **x and threads**: Short-form is where the metric is weakest. Below roughly 250 words a single item carries too little signal, which is another argument for batch scoring rather than per-post.
- **video and audio formats**: Out of scope for stylometry on the script, mostly — spoken register differs enough from written that scoring a script against a written corpus produces noise. Build a separate corpus from transcripts if this matters.
- **format note**: Long-form (articles, newsletters) gives the metric the most to work with and is also where voice is most visible to readers. Short reactive posts are simultaneously the hardest to score and the least consequential to get wrong.

**scales with**

- **caps**:
  - SIZE OF THE EXISTING CORPUS, and it is the binding constraint. A corpus can only be built from writing that already exists. Fifteen posts is a floor, 25-30 per cell is trustworthy, 50-200 is comfortable. Nothing accelerates this except having written.
  - NUMBER OF CELLS, multiplicatively and painfully. Two brands × two languages = four independent corpora, four thresholds, four score series. Each cell needs its own 25-30 posts, so scope creep here is expensive in a way that is invisible at design time.
  - DRAFTING BATCH SIZE. The metric requires ≥5 drafts per scoring run in the same cell. At 15 posts a month across four cells that is an awkward fit that must be DESIGNED FOR, not discovered: batch the drafting so five or more drafts in the same cell exist at once.
  - CADENCE, in both directions. Too slow and the corpus never fills; too fast and you cannot batch coherently. Roughly 10-20 posts a month in one or two cells is the sweet spot for this machinery.
  - TEAM SIZE, inverted. A solo writer IS the voice. Add a second writer and 'the corpus' becomes an average of two people, which is a different and mushier object.
- **does not scale with**: Follower count, budget or model quality. A 200-follower writer with four years of posts has a better corpus than a 50,000-follower account that has been ghostwritten. Model quality is explicitly ruled out by PersonalBench's 0.024 method spread — a better model does not get you closer to your own voice.
- **the objective asymmetry**: For CITATION visibility, voice barely matters — engines select on evidence density and self-containment, not on authorial fingerprint. For VIRALITY it matters more, through the recognition-and-retention channel. So voice work is worth most to someone whose primary objective is audience relationship, and close to nothing to someone optimizing purely for AI citation. Price it accordingly.
- **the compounding input nobody starts early enough**: Corpus collection. Every week without archiving published posts in full text, tagged by brand and language, is a week of reference material reconstructed by hand later. It is an hour of work to start and it compounds with delay in a way nothing else in this research does.

#### risk

**failure modes**

- **scoring single posts**: The most likely failure and the most damaging. Single-post AUC 0.76 means a per-post gate is wrong roughly a quarter of the time. Several false rejections a month, and the gate is switched off within a quarter. Batch five or more.
- **the polish tokenisation bug**: faststylometry's default tok_match_pattern r'^[a-z][a-z]+$' silently drops every diacritic-bearing Polish word and returns confident numbers from a mutilated vocabulary. No error, no warning. Override it and add a startup assertion.
- **pooling languages**: Computing a combined voice score across PL and EN. The two Deltas are different measurements sharing a name; averaging them produces a number that means nothing and moves for reasons nobody can trace.
- **regression to the corpus mean**: Treating the score as an objective to maximise. Genuine human writing varies — a technical teardown and a personal reflection are both authentically yours. A gate calibrated on a narrow slice rejects the good outliers and pushes every draft toward the mean, producing text that is unmistakably yours and progressively duller. Calibrate on a deliberately VARIED sample; set the threshold to catch the bottom decile; review rejections rather than trusting them.
- **using an llm judge**: It looks rigorous, it is cheap, it correlates with topic rather than style, and it will pass the generic drafts the gate exists to catch. Semantic embeddings fail the same way for the same reason.
- **hard gating before calibration**: Running it build-failing before the ROC exists. Guaranteed false rejections, permanent loss of trust. Advisory first, build-failing only after 30-50 genuine and 30-50 impostor batches per cell.
- **corpus contamination**: Including ghostwritten, heavily-edited or translated posts as canonical. The gate then certifies conformance to a voice that is partly someone else's — and it will pass exactly the drafts it should reject.
- **expecting it to fix generation**: The gate catches gross voice failures. It does not make the generator better, and PersonalBench says nothing at inference time will. Relying on the score to substitute for the human editor is the failure this entry most wants to prevent.

**ai slop risk**

- **risk level**: Moderate, and in an unexpected direction — the risk is not that the gate produces slop but that it produces MONOTONY, which is a different and quieter failure.
- **the distinction that matters**: An anti-slop gate asks 'does this contain the tells of machine writing?' — a property of the text in isolation. A voice gate asks 'is this close to the reference corpus?' — a property of the text relative to a person. A draft can be entirely free of AI tells and still sound nothing like you (competent, generic, wrong voice), and it can sound like you while carrying a few tells. Run both: the slop gate as a hard 0/1 rejection on tells, the voice gate as a batch-level floor.
- **the specific tell this practice creates**: Self-parody. A model conditioned hard on fifteen of your posts will reproduce your most distinctive surface habits — the em-dash, the one-line paragraph, the signature opener — at higher frequency than you actually use them. The output reads as an impression of you rather than as you: recognisable, slightly too much, and hollow where the specifics should be. The tell is stylistic markers present and substance absent.
- **the second tell**: Corpus-mean prose. Every post landing in the safe middle of your range, no outliers, no experiments, no post that sounds unlike the last twenty. Readers experience this as the author becoming boring, which is harder to diagnose than slop because nothing is obviously wrong with any individual post.
- **polish specific gap**: The anti-slop half is weaker in Polish — sloptrim is English-only and Polish slop detection has to be reconstructed from Vale regex and LanguageTool. The voice half is the STRONGER one for Polish, since Delta works natively once the diacritics pattern is fixed. So in Polish the voice gate carries more of the load than it does in English, which is an argument for building it first if Polish is a primary language.

**human input required**

- **the non substitutable contribution**: THE SUBSTANCE, and the voice gate makes its absence measurable rather than solving it. The gate confirms a draft sounds like you. It cannot confirm the draft SAYS anything — and the characteristic failure of a well-conditioned model is prose that is stylistically perfect and substantively empty.
- **the second non substitutable contribution**: CORPUS CURATION. Deciding what counts as canonical you — which posts are your voice, which are off-register experiments, which were not really written by you — is a judgement no metric can make, and it determines everything downstream. Get it wrong and the gate enforces the wrong target with full confidence.
- **the third**: THE THRESHOLD. Where to cut is a risk-appetite decision, not a statistical one. The ROC curve gives you the trade-off; only a human decides which false-accept rate is acceptable.
- **the checkable gate**: Two questions per post, both answerable in seconds. (1) Name one thing in this post that could only have come from me — a number, a client, a failure, a judgement with a reason. (2) Did a human read this end to end and could they defend every claim in it? If (1) is empty the post is stylistically-correct filler; if (2) is no, the Art. 50(4) editorial posture is gone along with the quality.
- **why the ceiling makes this load bearing**: PersonalBench's finding that no inference-time method reaches even the similarity between two DIFFERENT humans means a passing voice score is not evidence of authenticity. The gate's honest job is to catch gross failures; the human editor catches the rest, and always will. Set the threshold to fail the bottom decile, not to chase the human floor.

**detectability and disclosure**

- **is your own voice cloning detectable**: Practically, no — and the theory says it will stay that way. AI-assisted text that a human has edited is weakly detectable at best: detector AUROC is bounded by the shrinking distance between human and AI text distributions, and a human editing pass removes whatever statistical signal survived. Conditioning on your own corpus moves output TOWARD the human distribution, which if anything reduces detectability further. There is no C2PA manifest for a post body and no watermark that survives your rewrite.
- **what IS detectable**: Behavioural patterns, not textual ones. Platform classifiers see posting cadence, template repetition, near-duplicate structure across posts and accounts, and engagement anomalies. LinkedIn's reported ~97% accuracy on engagement-pod detection is the shape of what a graph-aware classifier can do. Text that is genuinely varied and specific survives; mass-produced output gets caught by the behavioural half regardless of how clean the prose is — which is the case for the voice gate being a floor with variety preserved, not a conformance maximiser.
- **the asymmetry for this entry**: Entirely on the low-detectability side of the divide. This is a TEXT tactic with no imagery, so C2PA and SynthID do not touch it and no auto-labeling exposure arises. (See the sibling entry 'Platform AI labeling and C2PA provenance'.) Do not let that be read as 'therefore disclosure does not matter' — it means the disclosure question here is ethical and legal, not technical.
- **disclosure triggered for your own voice**: None, in any jurisdiction, for using a model to help write in your own style with your own substance under your own editorial control. EU AI Act Art. 50(4)'s text obligation attaches only to AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, and is disapplied by substantive human review with editorial responsibility — which is exactly the posture this entry builds. No platform rule prohibits stylistic conditioning on your own corpus.
- **where the line is**: Cloning SOMEONE ELSE'S voice is a categorically different act. Publishing text in another identifiable person's style, presented as theirs, is impersonation — a platform violation everywhere, and depending on framing a personality-rights, passing-off or defamation matter rather than an AI-law one. The technology in this entry is symmetric; the ethics and the law are not. Keep the corpus to writing you authored.
- **the corpus is itself sensitive**: An exemplar corpus is a detailed behavioural profile of an identified individual, and it is the single input another party would need to imitate you. That is a commercial argument for keeping it local, independent of any privacy rule.

**policy and legal**

- **jurisdiction assumed**: Poland / EU.
- **eu ai act**: Art. 50 applies from 2026-08-02. Nothing in this entry triggers it for own-voice writing: no deepfake (text only), and the public-interest text obligation is disapplied by human review with editorial control, which the Commission FAQ defines as substantive examination by a knowledgeable person with authority to approve, alter or reject. Note that a person generating regular economic benefit from the activity IS a deployer — the personal/non-professional exclusion does not cover a consultant posting for leads — so the exemption you rely on is the editorial-review one, not the non-professional one. That is precisely why the gate must stay a filter and never a licence to publish unread.
- **gdpr**: The strongest privacy posture available if built locally: the corpus, the draft and the score never leave the machine — no processor, no transfer, no DPA, no residency question. This matters more than it first appears, because the corpus is a detailed behavioural profile of an identified individual and consultancy posts routinely name clients and colleagues. Every commercial alternative requires shipping exactly that corpus to a US vendor.
- **licensing of the stack**: Clean. mStyleDistance is MIT (base model FacebookAI/xlm-roberta-base); faststylometry is open source; Burrows's Delta is a published method with no owner. No AGPL, no Elastic 2.0, no Sustainable Use License anywhere in the primary path — the whole stack is redistributable inside a commercial product.
- **two checks beyond the primary path**: PAN@CLEF corpora carry research-oriented terms that should be read before publishing any derived benchmark (private threshold calibration is unproblematic). And if Markup AI is ever reconsidered, its numeric scoring is a per-organisation FEATURE FLAG rather than a documented entitlement of the tier you would buy — pin that down in writing rather than inferring it from a pricing page.
- **content rights in your own corpus**: Your published posts are yours to analyse. Republishing the assembled corpus is not the risk — it is already public — but transmitting it to a third-party scoring service, or letting it become training data, hands a competitor the single input needed to imitate the brand. Internal-analysis-only is the right posture for commercial reasons before it is one for legal reasons.
- **platform terms**: No platform API is touched by the primary path, so no ToS question arises and no account can be lost to the tooling.

**reversibility and blast radius**

- **ban risk**: None from the tooling. No accounts are touched, no API is called, nothing is scraped.
- **the residual risk runs opposite to intuition**: It is self-inflicted quality, not enforcement. A gate tuned too tightly rejects legitimate range and converges your writing on the corpus mean — unmistakably yours and progressively duller. That degradation is slow, invisible in any metric you are tracking (the voice score goes UP as this happens), and only noticed by readers who drift away without saying why.
- **reversibility of that failure**: Recoverable but slow. Loosening the threshold restores the gate immediately; restoring an audience's interest after six months of flattened writing takes longer than it took to lose.
- **the irreversible organisational failure**: Shipping the gate as build-failing before calibration. False rejections in the first weeks destroy trust permanently — a gate people learn to override has ceased to exist and cannot be reinstated by fixing the threshold.
- **corpus loss**: A real and overlooked risk. The corpus is the asset; it lives in your repo; back it up outside the platform it came from. Platforms change export policies and delete old content.
- **blast radius summary**: Small, local and entirely self-inflicted. This is the lowest-blast-radius entry in the whole table — nothing here can cost you an account, a fine or a public correction. The worst case is quietly becoming a duller writer, which is a real cost but a private one.

#### practice

**how to apply**

- **step 0 start the archive today**: Before any tooling: archive every published post, full text, tagged by (brand, language, date, platform). One hour of setup. This is the only step with a compounding cost of delay, and a corpus can only be built from writing that exists. Do this even if you never build the rest.
- **step 1 curate the corpus**:
  - Triage every archived post into canonical / off-register / not-really-mine. Exclude the third category absolutely; keep deliberate variety within the first.
  - Split by cell: (brand, language). Do not merge cells whose registers differ by design — a SaaS voice and a personal consulting voice are different registers, which is the whole reason a gate exists.
  - Target 25-30 posts per cell before trusting any number; 15 (~5,000 words) is the absolute floor from Eder and it is optimistic as applied to pooled short posts.
  - Version the corpus as a single corpus_id. Stamp it on every score.
- **step 2 extract a style spec**: Run the style-spec extraction prompt with the evidence requirement. Keep the output in .claude/skills/brand-voice-generator/ or an equivalent versioned location. Review it yourself — a spec you disagree with is a spec built on a contaminated corpus.
- **step 3 build the metric**:
  - Wrap faststylometry. FIRST ACTION: override tok_match_pattern and add a startup assertion that fails loudly if the default pattern is active on a non-English corpus. This bug silently invalidates every Polish number.
  - Use predict_proba() so the output is a calibrated probability, not an arbitrary distance.
  - Optionally benchmark mStyleDistance against Delta on the same held-out set and decide whether the second signal earns its place. Do not adopt it as primary — Delta's zero continuity risk is why it leads.
- **step 4 calibrate the threshold**:
  - Positives: your genuine posts, grouped into batches of five from the same cell.
  - Negatives: impostor drafts on the same topics, generated with the same models you will actually use. Free, unlimited, and the only way to answer the question no published benchmark answers.
  - Compute Delta for both, plot the ROC, choose the cut-off at a false-accept rate you can live with. 30-50 batches per side per cell.
  - Calibrate Polish more conservatively than English and expect a wider uncertain band — PAN@CLEF 2018 found Polish the hardest of five languages at best macro-F1 0.556.
  - Optional external check: PAN@CLEF 2018 as a free independent Polish authorship benchmark alongside your own set.
- **step 5 wire it as a gate**:
  - Score BATCHES of five or more drafts from the same cell. Never a single post. Fix the batch size in configuration.
  - Two independent score series named voice_delta_pl and voice_delta_en. Encode the language in the NAME so no dashboard can pool them.
  - Run ADVISORY for four weeks. Log every score, review every would-be rejection by hand. Switch to build-failing only when you agree with the gate's judgement more often than not.
  - Set the threshold to fail the bottom decile, not to chase the human floor.
- **step 6 batch the drafting**: The metric needs ≥5 drafts per cell per run, and the cost arithmetic independently rewards clustering calls inside the cache TTL (about $0.40/month batched vs $2.81/month spread, on Opus 5 with a 30k-token corpus). One workflow change satisfies both. Budget for the conversation about batching, not for the code — it is the part most likely to be resisted.
- **step 7 persist and watch for drift**: Write each score as a named score on the draft trace in whatever observability layer exists, so drift becomes a visible time series rather than an impression. The score is computed at T+0 and is final — the easiest score in any pipeline to persist.
- **step 8 the one delayed analysis worth running**: Correlate the T+0 voice score against T+7 reach. This is not engagement prediction; it is post-hoc attribution, and it is the ONLY way to test the working assumption that sounding like yourself actually helps on a platform now suppressing generic content. Do not expect an answer inside a year at 15 posts a month.

**checklist**

- **gate type**: Pass/fail before a batch ships. Applies to the BATCH, not the post.
- **items**:
  - [ ] This score was computed on a batch of FIVE OR MORE drafts from the same (brand, language) cell. (FAIL on a single-post score — AUC 0.76 vs 0.96 is the whole reason.)
  - [ ] The corpus for this cell has at least 25 posts. (WARN at 15-24; FAIL below 15 / ~5,000 words.)
  - [ ] faststylometry's token pattern was overridden and the startup assertion passed. (FAIL — a default-pattern Polish score is confident and wrong.)
  - [ ] The score series is language-named (voice_delta_pl / voice_delta_en) and no combined score exists anywhere in the pipeline. (FAIL on any pooled number.)
  - [ ] corpus_id, model revision and batch size are stamped on this score. (FAIL if any is missing — all three change the number.)
  - [ ] The threshold was set from an ROC on ≥30 genuine and ≥30 impostor batches for THIS cell. (FAIL on a guessed threshold; run advisory until it exists.)
  - [ ] No number in this score came from an LLM judge or a semantic embedding model. (FAIL is terminal.)
  - [ ] Each post in the batch contains at least one thing only I could have written — a number, a client, a failure, a judgement with a reason. (FAIL on stylistically-correct filler; the voice gate cannot catch this and it is the most common real failure.)
  - [ ] A human read each post end to end and can defend every claim. (FAIL — this is the quality gate and the Art. 50(4) editorial posture in one line.)
  - [ ] The threshold is set to fail the bottom decile, not to maximise similarity. (WARN if the mean score has been rising for three months — that is convergence on the corpus mean, not improvement.)

#### measurement

**kpis and leading indicators**

- **primary kpi**: voice_delta_pl and voice_delta_en as two independent time series, one point per scored batch, stamped with corpus_id, model revision and batch size. Read as DRIFT over time, not as a level — the absolute number is meaningless outside its calibration.
- **secondary**:
  - Gate block rate. A stable low rate (roughly one batch in ten) means the gate is doing work. Zero forever means it is not running or the threshold is too loose. Rising means either the generator or the corpus has drifted.
  - Manual-agreement rate on blocked batches. Review every block; if you disagree with more than half, the threshold is wrong and the gate is losing trust.
  - Corpus coverage per cell — posts archived, against the 25-30 target. The only KPI here that predicts whether the system will work at all.
  - Score VARIANCE within a batch, not just the mean. Falling variance is convergence on the corpus mean — the monotony failure — and it shows up in variance long before anyone notices the writing got duller.
- **leading indicators**:
  - Corpus archive freshness: days since the last published post was added. Silent decay starts here.
  - Drafts-per-batch actually achieved. Falling below five means the gate is about to be run on unreliable single-post scores or skipped entirely.
  - Model revision changes. A version bump invalidates score comparability across the boundary; treat it as a new series rather than a continuation.
  - The mean score trending steadily UP over months. Counter-intuitively a warning, not a success — it is the signature of convergence on the corpus mean.
- **what not to track**: Any pooled cross-language 'voice score'. Also any attempt to correlate voice score with reach on fewer than a year of data — the sample is far too small and the temptation to read a pattern into it is strong.
